Question 1

A company delivers registration first, then adds payments and reporting, each as a usable delivery. Which model specifically names this addition-of-functionality strategy, independent of whether earlier features are also refined?

  • A. Waterfall
  • B. Incremental
  • C. Spiral
  • D. Evolutionary

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 3

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: B — Incremental

The delivery strategy adds usable capabilities in stages so that end users receive a valuable subset before the complete product is ready. Incremental development names that addition of functionality. Evolutionary development broadly emphasizes refinement and can overlap with increments, but does not specifically name the stated delivery distinction. Spiral is organized around risk-reduction cycles, and classical waterfall normally delays usable delivery until its planned development phases are complete.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose incremental delivery when prioritized partial capability must reach users early. Smaller changes can be easier to debug and permit feedback, though architecture and integration still require planning. Iteration need not rebuild the whole system every time, and increments need not be perfectly independent modules. Broad descriptions of early working software can fit prototypes, iterative or Agile processes; identify the purpose of that early version.SE04
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall organizes sequential phases rather than prioritizing staged usable subsets.

B · correct — Incremental development adds usable capability in successive deliveries.

C · incorrect — Spiral names risk-driven cycles; those may contain increments without defining this delivery strategy.

D · incorrect — Evolutionary refinement can overlap with increments, but the question asks the specific name for adding usable functionality.

Question 2

If you want to test individual sub-systems of software, which phase of software testing is appropriate?

  • A. Integration testing
  • B. Unit testing
  • C. System testing
  • D. Acceptance testing

Source

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 10

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

Correct answer: B — Unit testing

Unit testing tests isolated building blocks, including objects and subsystems; integration begins when individually tested components are combined.

Evidence in the complete study note

Acceptance testing supports the customer/user’s acceptance decision against agreed needs and criteria. Alpha typically happens in a controlled developer setting with selected users; beta uses external users in their environments. None of these levels is universally the longest. Unit is a level, while white-box is a technique; a unit can be tested using black-box cases too.SE35

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Combines components rather than isolating a subsystem. See PDF p. 148, 144.

B · correct — Directly tests an individual object or subsystem. See PDF p. 148, 144.

C · incorrect — Tests components together as one system. See PDF p. 148, 144.

D · incorrect — Checks the delivered system against the client agreement. See PDF p. 148, 144.

Question 3

Which characteristic of requirements specifies that the requirement should be phrased so that there is one and only one interpretation for it?

  • A. Unambiguous
  • B. Correct
  • C. Feasible
  • D. Verifiable

Sources

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 19

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 12

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Correct answer: A — Unambiguous

A single interpretation is the unambiguous property. Correctness, feasibility and verifiability answer different questions.

Evidence in the complete study note

Correct requirements reflect actual stakeholder needs. Complete requirements address the agreed scope, normal and exceptional behavior. Consistency excludes contradictions. Clarity/unambiguity gives one intended interpretation; feasibility/realism means achievable within constraints. Verifiability means objective evidence can check fulfillment. Replace “fast for most users” with a defined metric, workload and threshold.SE11

Choice by choice

A · correct — Rules out two or more interpretations. See PDF p. 68, 70.

B · incorrect — Accuracy to the client's view does not guarantee a unique reading. See PDF p. 68, 70.

C · incorrect — Realism concerns implementation within constraints. See PDF p. 68, 70.

D · incorrect — Requires a repeatable test, not a unique interpretation alone. See PDF p. 68, 70.

Question 4

Which option most completely summarizes the listed observable behaviors that functional requirements may specify?

  • A. specifies the tasks the program must complete
  • B. Specifies observable tasks the program must not perform
  • C. Specifies required observable responses to invalid input
  • D. All of the mentioned

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 82

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

Correct answer: D — All of the mentioned

Functional requirements describe observable services and behavior, including what must happen, what is prohibited and how the system responds to errors. Each individual choice gives one of these forms. The all-of-the-mentioned option is therefore the complete summary. Selecting only A, B or C would omit other valid functional obligations; negative wording alone does not make a requirement nonfunctional.

Evidence in the complete study note

A functional requirement states an observable service or behavior, including reactions to inputs, errors and forbidden actions. “When the sensor detects intrusion, send an alert” is functional. “Only a manager may approve refunds” also specifies permitted/prohibited behavior. A negative statement is not automatically nonfunctional.SE09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Required tasks are functional, but A alone omits the other listed forms.

B · incorrect — Prohibited tasks can be functional, but B alone is incomplete.

C · incorrect — Required error responses are functional, but C alone is incomplete.

D · correct — All three listed observable behavior forms can be functional requirements.

Question 5

A team has little experience with a project’s unfamiliar technology. Major feasibility risks must be evaluated before each further commitment, and experienced risk-analysis support is available. Which lifecycle is selected specifically by that risk-driven criterion?

  • A. Iterative Enhancement Model
  • B. RAD
  • C. Spiral
  • D. Waterfall

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 83

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 95

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: C — Spiral

Spiral organizes each cycle around objectives, alternatives, risk assessment and reduction before further commitment. That directly addresses the specified major feasibility risks and supported risk-analysis capability. Iterative enhancement can aid learning but does not make risk assessment its defining organizer; RAD needs rapid construction and skilled support. Classical waterfall fits stable requirements and familiar technology, which the scenario does not supply.

Evidence in the complete study note

Select a process using requirement stability, technical risk, delivery urgency, stakeholder availability, team skills and assurance needs. “Team has little experience” alone does not uniquely identify a process. A risk-driven cycle, prototype or carefully planned staged process may each help, depending on the actual uncertainty. No process eliminates the need for testing or documentation.SE02
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Iteration supports feedback but is not defined by risk-driven commitments.

B · incorrect — RAD emphasizes rapid construction rather than the specified risk cycle.

C · correct — Spiral explicitly organizes commitment around major risk reduction.

D · incorrect — Unfamiliar technology and unresolved risks do not fit the stated classical waterfall rationale.

Question 6

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

Study-guide references

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

Correct answer: A — Development and Documentation

Programming translates the design into source code in implementation. A corresponds to the development stage of implementation and unit testing.

Evidence in the complete study note

A common lifecycle names requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance. Analysis clarifies the problem; system design chooses architecture; object/detail design specifies interfaces and algorithms; implementation writes code; testing evaluates behavior; deployment puts it into service. These activities may overlap and repeat.SE02

Question 7

Which offered requirement is nonfunctional, specifying a measurable quality rather than required or prohibited observable tasks?

  • A. specifies the tasks the program must complete
  • B. Specifies observable tasks the program must not perform
  • C. Specifies the required error response to invalid input
  • D. Search shall respond within two seconds under 100 concurrent users.

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 94

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Correct answer: D — Search shall respond within two seconds under 100 concurrent users.

The response-time limit under a defined concurrent-user workload is a measurable performance requirement, a nonfunctional quality constraint. Required services, prohibited actions and specified error responses are all forms of observable functional behavior. Their positive or negative wording does not determine the category. D instead constrains how well the search service must perform, making it the unique nonfunctional example.

Evidence in the complete study note

A functional requirement states an observable service or behavior, including reactions to inputs, errors and forbidden actions. “When the sensor detects intrusion, send an alert” is functional. “Only a manager may approve refunds” also specifies permitted/prohibited behavior. A negative statement is not automatically nonfunctional.SE09
“Search responds within two seconds under 100 concurrent users” is measurable performance. “New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability. “Use Java” is a technology/pseudo-requirement, often separately classified as a system constraint. Dependability includes reliability, safety and robustness; portability is not its usual central category. Performance degradation at peak load primarily concerns performance, not automatically reliability.SE10

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Required observable tasks are functional.

B · incorrect — Prohibited observable tasks can be functional.

C · incorrect — An observable error response specifies functional behavior.

D · correct — The time threshold and workload constrain performance quality.

Question 8

Which of the following is the understanding of software product limitations, learning system related problems or changes to be done in existing systems beforehand, identifying and addressing the impact of project on organization and personnel etc.?

  • A. Software Design
  • B. Feasibility Study
  • C. Requirement Gathering
  • D. System Analysis

Source

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 98

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

Correct answer: B — Feasibility study.

SE08 asks whether a proposal is worth doing and deliverable, considering existing limitations, impacts on organization and personnel, benefits, costs, skills and integration risk. That matches the stem’s preliminary impact and constraint investigation. System analysis studies the detailed problem and behavior and informs feasibility, but the broad early viability assessment is the more specific match here.

Evidence in the complete study note

Feasibility asks whether a proposal is worth doing and can be delivered within technical, economic, operational and schedule constraints. Examine existing limitations, organizational impacts, benefits, cost, available skills and integration risk. System analysis studies the problem and needed behavior in more detail; the activities inform each other.SE08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Design chooses solution structures rather than primarily assessing preliminary viability and organizational impacts.

B · correct — Feasibility investigates existing limitations, impacts and whether the proposal is worthwhile and deliverable.

C · incorrect — Gathering needs is useful input but does not by itself cover the full viability assessment.

D · incorrect — System analysis examines detailed problem behavior; feasibility is the more specific preliminary impact/viability activity.

Question 9

For a software product developed to meet a client’s requirements, which choice most completely describes its scope?

  • A. Software product refers any software created to meet the client's requirements.
  • B. Software product includes design and test documentation.
  • C. Software product includes requirement specifications, and user manuals.
  • D. All of the above

Adapted from

  • Addis Ababa University mock exam · Question 22

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Correct answer: D — All of the above

SE01 explicitly includes executable code plus requirements, designs, test assets, configuration and user documentation in a software product. A describes the implemented software, while B and C name relevant accompanying artifacts. All three descriptions are therefore compatible; none limits the product to code alone. D is the inclusive answer among these options.

Evidence in the complete study note

Software engineering applies systematic methods to development, operation and maintenance. A software product includes executable code and relevant requirements, designs, test assets, configuration and user documentation. A process defines activities, ordering, roles, products and entry/exit conditions. Its four broad activities are specification, design/implementation, validation and evolution.SE01

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Software built to meet client requirements forms part of the product.

B · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Relevant design and testing documentation are included product artifacts.

C · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Requirements specifications and user manuals are relevant product documentation.

D · correct — All three descriptions are compatible with the complete software-product scope.

Question 10

One of the followings is type of requirements associated with quality features of a software.

  • A. Business requirements

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Correct answer: C — Non-functional

Quality and user-visible constraints beyond functional behavior are nonfunctional requirements; user and business are viewpoints rather than this quality classification.

Evidence in the complete study note

Nonfunctional requirements include quality attributes and constraints. Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning. Question 11

A type of requirement that describes why the software project is needed and used to define the objective of the software is .

  • A. Business requirements
  • B. Functional requirements
  • C. Non-functional requirements
  • D. User requirements

Source

  • Addis Ababa University mock exam · Question 24

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

Correct answer: A — Business requirements.

SE08 distinguishes the business reason and objectives of a project from user needs and detailed system obligations. The question asks why the project is needed and what objectives it serves, so business requirements match directly. Functional requirements describe behavior, while nonfunctional requirements describe qualities or constraints; neither primarily states the project's business justification.

Evidence in the complete study note

Business requirements explain why the project exists and its goals. User requirements describe stakeholder needs at a useful high level; system requirements specify detailed services and constraints. The Software Requirements Specification (SRS) organizes the agreed requirements. A natural-language specification communicates with clients while analysis models formalize it for technical discussion; real specifications can also contain diagrams.SE08

Choice by choice

A · correct — Business requirements state the project's purpose, justification and intended organizational goals.

B · incorrect — Functional requirements specify observable system services rather than the overall business reason for the project.

C · incorrect — Nonfunctional requirements specify qualities or constraints rather than why the project exists.

D · incorrect — User requirements describe stakeholder needs at a high level rather than the project's business justification.

Question 12

Which of the following is used to model the functionality of software?

  • A. Use case diagram
  • B. Class diagram
  • C. E-R diagram
  • D. Deployment diagram

Source

  • Addis Ababa University mock exam · Question 25

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

SE-S03 · Modeling categories and data diagrams

SE24 · Architecture styles and integration boundaries

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

SE-S03 · Modeling categories and data diagrams

SE24 · Architecture styles and integration boundaries

Correct answer: A — Use case diagram

Use-case diagrams model external roles and their goals or interactions with the system. This is the functional view requested. Class diagrams instead emphasize static classes, features and relationships. Entity–relationship diagrams organize entity types, attributes and data relationships. Deployment diagrams map software artifacts to execution nodes. Each can contribute to understanding a system, but only the use-case view directly presents the actor-goal functionality in this comparison.

Evidence in the complete study note

Draw actors outside the system boundary rectangle and use-case ovals inside. Name a goal with a verb and noun. The diagram shows roles, goals and relationships, not the full detailed algorithm or UI layout. Being an internal component is different from being an external actor; the chosen boundary determines which role applies.SE14
An entity–relationship diagram models entity types, their attributes and the relationships between them, commonly for data design. Its focus differs from a use-case diagram of external roles and goals, a class diagram of classes and their features, or a deployment diagram mapping artifacts to execution nodes.SE-S03
A component diagram shows components/interfaces/dependencies; a deployment diagram places software artifacts on nodes.SE24

Choice by choice

A · correct — Use-case diagrams show external actors and the system goals they use.

B · incorrect — Class diagrams describe static types and their relationships.

C · incorrect — ER diagrams describe entity types, attributes and data relationships.

D · incorrect — Deployment diagrams map software artifacts onto execution nodes.

Question 13

Which of the following refers to the deployment platform? i

  • A. Use case
  • B. Tier
  • C. Layer
  • D. Component

Source

  • Addis Ababa University mock exam · Question 26

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Correct answer: B — Tier.

SE23 explicitly separates logical abstraction from deployment separation. A layer organizes responsibilities logically, whereas a tier describes their deployment separation or platform arrangement. A use case models an actor goal, and a component is a software building block. Neither is the term for the deployment distinction asked for here.

Evidence in the complete study note

A layer is a logical abstraction level; a tier is a deployment separation. A closed layered architecture permits calls only to the immediately lower layer; an open one permits approved skipping. For top-to-bottom A,B,C,D, A→B obeys closed layering, A→C skips, and lower-to-upper calls violate the simple dependency rule unless explicitly mediated by a defined mechanism.SE23

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A use case models a goal or interaction rather than the deployment platform separation.

B · correct — A tier identifies deployment separation, contrasting with logical layering.

C · incorrect — A layer is a logical abstraction level and need not occupy a distinct deployment platform.

D · incorrect — A component is a software element and does not itself denote a deployment tier.

Question 14

When requirements will change substantially and frequent early feedback is needed, which classical process organization is least accommodating among these choices?

  • A. Waterfall
  • B. Scrum
  • C. RAD
  • D. Agile

Adapted from

  • Addis Ababa University mock exam · Question 27

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Correct answer: A — Waterfall

Classical waterfall commits to planned phases and reviewed deliverables, making late feedback and changed requirements costly. Agile and Scrum plan and inspect work incrementally, allowing later content to adapt. RAD also uses rapid construction and user participation to obtain feedback. The comparison therefore favors waterfall as the least accommodating under the stated conditions, without claiming that a waterfall project is physically unable to authorize any change.

Evidence in the complete study note

Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03
Agile favors people collaborating, useful working results, customer participation and adaptation over rigid adherence to procedures, exhaustive documents, contracts or fixed plans. The latter still have value. Agile does not mean no planning or no documentation. A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05
A prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility. A throwaway prototype is discarded after learning; an evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. A quick prototype may omit robustness, security or architecture, so do not deploy it unchanged without evaluation. Coding may occur during prototyping even if a diagram labels that activity construction rather than coding.SE07

Choice by choice

A · correct — Late feedback and phase commitments make major requirement changes costly in classical waterfall.

B · incorrect — Scrum inspects usable increments and adapts later work within its planning framework.

C · incorrect — RAD uses rapid construction and user participation to obtain feedback.

D · incorrect — Agile explicitly values responding to changing needs.

Question 17

Which option combines both explicitly specified testability mechanisms among A, C and D? Treat refactoring alone as behavior-preserving restructuring with no stated testability improvement.

  • A. Sand box
  • B. A and D
  • C. Refactoring
  • D. Limiting structural complexity

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 42

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: B — A and D

A sandbox can isolate execution, giving control over the test environment. Limiting structural complexity also supports testability by making behavior easier to control and observe. Refactoring preserves behavior while changing structure, but without a stated improvement it does not automatically supply either testability effect. The combination A and D therefore includes both explicitly supported mechanisms; the individual choices each give only one.

Evidence in the complete study note

Variability can use selectable features, omission/inclusion and extension points; overloading supplies alternate signatures in code but is not every variability mechanism. Testability improves with controllable inputs, observable outputs, replaceable dependencies and limited structural complexity. A sandbox can isolate execution. Assess each design claim independently before evaluating a combined statement.SE27
Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Sandbox isolation is valid but only one of the two mechanisms.

B · correct — A and D include both explicitly supported mechanisms.

C · incorrect — Unspecified refactoring need not improve testability.

D · incorrect — Limited structural complexity is valid but only one of the two mechanisms.

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Correct answers (select all): B, C — Omission or inclusion of elements; Extension point

Omitting or including selected elements permits configured architectural variation, and extension points define places where additional behavior can be supplied. Overloading by itself supplies alternate code signatures and does not establish either architectural mechanism. Thus B and C meet the specified architectural scope. The all-of-the-above choice includes that insufficient code-level case and therefore cannot be selected as a correct aggregate.

Evidence in the complete study note

Variability can use selectable features, omission/inclusion and extension points; overloading supplies alternate signatures in code but is not every variability mechanism. Testability improves with controllable inputs, observable outputs, replaceable dependencies and limited structural complexity. A sandbox can isolate execution. Assess each design claim independently before evaluating a combined statement.SE27

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Alternate signatures alone do not define the specified architectural variability.

B · correct — Selectable omission or inclusion changes architectural configuration.

C · correct — Extension points explicitly support variation at defined boundaries.

D · incorrect — It incorrectly includes overloading alone as an architectural mechanism.

Question 19

Which choice most completely describes the stated advantages of the Factory Method pattern?

  • A. Allows the sub-classes to choose the type of objects to create
  • B. Promotes loose coupling
  • C. A and B
  • D. None of the above

Study-guide sections

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Correct answer: C — A and B

SE27 describes Factory Method as letting subclasses choose a concrete product through a creation operation, reducing dependence on concrete constructors. Those are exactly the two benefits in A and B, so C is the inclusive answer. The reference is to Factory Method; a simple factory is related but does not necessarily delegate product choice to subclasses.

Evidence in the complete study note

Factory Method lets subclasses choose a concrete product through a creation operation, reducing coupling to concrete constructors. A simple factory centralizes creation but is not identical to Factory Method. Singleton controls access to one instance; Observer notifies subscribers; Memento stores/restores state while hiding representation; Iterator traverses; Decorator adds behavior through wrapping. The pattern name is Memento, not Momento.SE27

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Factory Method lets subclasses select the concrete product through the creation operation.

B · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Depending on the creation abstraction reduces coupling to concrete product constructors.

C · correct — Both listed benefits hold for Factory Method, making this the inclusive answer.

D · incorrect — The note explicitly supports both benefits, so none is false.

Question 20

Which statements correctly distinguish architectural structures and views? Select all that apply.

  • A. B and D only
  • B. Views design structures whereas architects document the structures.
  • C. A structure is the set of elements and their relations as they exist in software or hardware.
  • D. A view is a representation of a structure

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 45

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Correct answers (select all): C, D — A structure is the set of elements and their relations as they exist in software or hardware.; A view is a representation of a structure

An architectural structure consists of elements and their relations in the modeled software or hardware. A view represents selected aspects of a structure for a particular purpose. Both C and D therefore express compatible definitions. Views are representations, not agents that design structures, so B is false. The aggregate A includes that false statement and incorrectly excludes the true structure definition.

Evidence in the complete study note

A structure is the elements/relations themselves; a view represents selected aspects. Module structures show code organization, component-and-connector structures runtime interaction, and allocation structures map software to hardware, teams or environment. Processes/threads belong in concurrency views. Evaluate architectures against quality attributes and scenarios; processor allocation, decomposition and style selection can all be architectural concerns.SE23

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The B-and-D-only combination includes false B and excludes true C.

B · incorrect — Views represent structures rather than acting as their designers.

C · correct — A structure is the underlying set of elements and relations.

D · correct — A view represents selected aspects of a structure.

Question 21

Which testing level isolates one function or class, using stubs or mocks for called dependencies, so its internal branches can be tested directly?

  • A. System testing
  • B. Integration testing
  • C. System and integration testing together
  • D. Unit testing

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 46

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: D — Unit testing

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component and may replace dependencies with stubs or mocks. That matches the stated test scope. White-box cases can then target its internal branches, but white-box is a technique rather than a testing level. Integration and system tests cover combined interactions or the full system, so neither matches the isolation specified here.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35
Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — System testing evaluates the complete integrated system.

B · incorrect — Integration testing targets interactions among combined parts.

C · incorrect — Combining system and integration levels does not give isolated unit scope.

D · correct — Unit testing isolates the function or class with replaceable dependencies.

Question 22

Which offered UML diagram models external behavioral goals and actor interactions at a high level, rather than detailed message timing or state evolution?

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

Correct answer: B — Use case diagram

A use-case diagram presents external roles, their goals and relationships within a chosen system boundary. It therefore matches the specified high-level behavioral scope. Component, deployment and class diagrams describe structural organization, allocation or static types. Sequence, activity and state diagrams would be appropriate for detailed interactions, workflows or state changes, but those finer-grained dynamic questions are explicitly outside this stem.

Evidence in the complete study note

An activity diagram models workflow: filled circle start, rounded actions, guarded decision diamond, thick fork/join bars and partitions/swimlanes for responsibility. A diamond can also merge alternative flows; a join synchronizes concurrent flows. A state machine models states and transitions triggered by events, often with guards/actions, for one object’s lifecycle.SE20
Draw actors outside the system boundary rectangle and use-case ovals inside. Name a goal with a verb and noun. The diagram shows roles, goals and relationships, not the full detailed algorithm or UI layout. Being an internal component is different from being an external actor; the chosen boundary determines which role applies.SE14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Component diagrams describe components and interfaces.

B · correct — Use-case diagrams show actor roles and high-level goals.

C · incorrect — Deployment diagrams allocate artifacts to nodes.

D · incorrect — Class diagrams show static types and relationships.

Question 23

Which choice most completely identifies the listed reasons requirements elicitation can be difficult?

  • A. All choices are correct
  • B. Problem of scope
  • C. Problem of understanding
  • D. Problem of volatility

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 48

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

SE-S01 · Scope, understanding and changing requirements

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

SE-S01 · Scope, understanding and changing requirements

Correct answer: A — All choices are correct

SE11 identifies scope, understanding and volatility as distinct elicitation difficulties. Scope concerns agreeing what belongs in the system; understanding concerns discovering and interpreting actual needs; volatility concerns needs changing as the project progresses. Since all three listed problems are valid, the inclusive answer is appropriate rather than choosing just one source of difficulty.

Evidence in the complete study note

Correct requirements reflect actual stakeholder needs. Complete requirements address the agreed scope, normal and exceptional behavior. Consistency excludes contradictions. Clarity/unambiguity gives one intended interpretation; feasibility/realism means achievable within constraints. Verifiability means objective evidence can check fulfillment. Replace “fast for most users” with a defined metric, workload and threshold.SE11
Trace each requirement backward to its source/rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Record dependencies among requirements. A traceability matrix links these artifacts and helps impact analysis; it is not just a cost/schedule ledger. Stakeholders must negotiate conflicting requirements rather than independently approving incompatible demands. Scope, understanding and volatility are distinct elicitation difficulties.SE11
Elicitation difficulties have several distinct sources. Scope problems concern agreeing on system boundaries and the appropriate level of detail. Understanding problems arise when stakeholders and analysts have different domain knowledge, omit tacit needs or communicate conflicting interpretations. Volatility means that requirements change as circumstances and understanding develop.SE-S01
These difficulties call for repeated communication, explicit boundaries, negotiated meanings and controlled revision. They can occur together; resolving one does not automatically remove the others.SE-S01

Choice by choice

A · correct — All three listed difficulties are explicitly recognized in the complete note.

B · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Unclear system boundaries make agreeing on included and excluded requirements difficult.

C · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Different interpretations and tacit stakeholder needs complicate accurate understanding.

D · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Changing needs make elicitation an ongoing activity rather than a one-time capture.

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

Correct answer: C — Analysis

Analysis clarifies the problem, required behavior and constraints. Design then chooses architecture, interfaces and algorithms for a solution; implementation writes it, and testing evaluates its behavior. The revised scope keeps these responsibilities distinct instead of mixing problem recognition with selecting methods to overcome it. Creativity can occur in several activities, so the activity’s purpose, rather than that adjective, determines the answer.

A common lifecycle names requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance. Analysis clarifies the problem; system design chooses architecture; object/detail design specifies interfaces and algorithms; implementation writes code; testing evaluates behavior; deployment puts it into service. These activities may overlap and repeat.SE02

Question 26

Which structural risk can arise when repeated software changes are made without coherent design or refactoring?

  • A. Reduced user engagement
  • B. Increased software complexity
  • C. Increased automation
  • D. Elimination of maintenance costs

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 51

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk.

Study-guide sections

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

Correct answer: B — Increased software complexity

Repeated changes without coherent boundaries can accumulate dependencies and make the evolving system harder to understand. Refactoring and good subsystem design help control that structural complexity while maintenance still requires impact analysis and regression checks. User engagement is a product-use outcome rather than the structural risk asked for. Automation is an execution technique, not itself structural deterioration, and ongoing evolution does not eliminate maintenance costs.

Evidence in the complete study note

Software engineering applies systematic methods to development, operation and maintenance. A software product includes executable code and relevant requirements, designs, test assets, configuration and user documentation. A process defines activities, ordering, roles, products and entry/exit conditions. Its four broad activities are specification, design/implementation, validation and evolution.SE01
Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40
Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22
poor object design can still be complex.SE01
Refactor to preserve behavior while improving structure; optimize only against measured needs; record rationale and update traceability and regression evidence after change.SE43

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Engagement concerns user behavior rather than the internal structural deterioration asked for.

B · correct — Accumulated poorly coordinated changes can increase structural complexity.

C · incorrect — Automation does not itself describe deterioration of responsibilities or dependency structure.

D · incorrect — Changing software still requires maintenance and regression work.

Question 27

Which of the following best describes the difference between CPM and PERT?

  • A. CPM focuses on minimizing cost, while PERT focuses on minimizing time.
  • B. CPM is used for projects with uncertain activity durations, while PERT is used for projects with known activity durations.
  • C. PERT is used for projects with uncertain activity durations, while CPM is used for projects with known activity durations.
  • D. PERT is deterministic, whereas CPM is probabilistic.

Source

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 52

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Correct answer: C — PERT models uncertain durations; traditional CPM uses point durations.

SE30 gives traditional CPM point estimates and PERT optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic duration estimates. PERT therefore represents duration uncertainty, whereas the traditional CPM calculation uses known or fixed activity durations. The cost-versus-time contrast is not the defining distinction here, and the other two choices reverse the described treatment of uncertainty.

Evidence in the complete study note

Traditional CPM uses point durations; PERT models uncertainty with optimistic a, most-likely m and pessimistic b. The classic estimate is TE=(a+4m+b)/6 and variance=((b-a)/6)^2. For 3,6,15 days, TE=42/6=7 days and variance=4 days². Do not replace the weighted estimate by a simple average. These formulas are approximations, not guaranteed actual completion times.SE30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The note's defining contrast concerns duration uncertainty rather than assigning cost exclusively to CPM.

B · incorrect — This reverses the models: PERT explicitly represents uncertain activity durations.

C · correct — PERT uses uncertain three-point estimates, while traditional CPM uses fixed point durations.

D · incorrect — The probabilistic/deterministic characterization is reversed relative to the note.

SE28 · Planning, WBS, estimation and tools

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE28 · Planning, WBS, estimation and tools

Correct answer: C — Improved team communication and collaboration.

SE28 says planning tools coordinate ownership, dependencies and progress while leaving judgment to people. That coordination supports communication and collaboration. The tool does not automatically detect and repair code faults, replace project managers or directly guarantee faster coding. Those benefits would require other capabilities and evidence beyond project-management tooling itself.

Evidence in the complete study note

Planning is continuous: identify scope/deliverables, decompose work, estimate effort/duration/cost, assign resources, sequence dependencies and revise as evidence changes. A WBS is hierarchical and covers project scope without adding unrelated work. Tools help coordinate ownership, dependencies and progress; they do not replace judgment or automatically fix bugs.SE28

B · incorrect — They support planning and coordination while human managers still supply judgment.

D · incorrect — A direct increase in coding efficiency is not the general coordination benefit established here.

A project team is working on a software project with multiple developers. They decided to implement a version control system (VCS). Which of the following scenarios best describes the use case for a distributed VCS like Git?

  • A. The team prefers to avoid merge conflicts by locking files so only one developer can work on a file at a time.
  • B. The team is large, geographically distributed, and each developer needs to work on features independently and merge changes later.
  • C. The team is small, and all developers work in the same physical location on a single branch.

  • Mock exam 4 · Question 56

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate artifact history and controlled changes from scheduling, collaboration benefits and automated execution.

Study-guide sections

SE33 · Configuration, change control and version control

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE33 · Configuration, change control and version control

Correct answer: B — Independent distributed development followed by merging.

SE33 says a distributed Git clone contains local history and allows independent branches that can later be merged. B matches that working arrangement directly. Git does not require everyone to lock files, use one local branch or obtain central permission before every local commit. Additional review policies can be imposed, but they do not define distributed version control.

Change management handles request, impact assessment, decision/prioritization, implementation and validation; configuration management keeps all affected versions consistent. Plan test configuration management early and apply it throughout testing, not at just one exclusive phase.SE33

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Exclusive file locking is not the defining distributed Git collaboration model.

B · correct — Local histories and independent branches support geographically distributed work followed by merging.

C · incorrect — A colocated team can use Git, but this scenario does not express its independent distributed-work benefit.

D · incorrect — Central approval policies can exist, but they do not define or require distributed local commits.

Study-guide references

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

The SRS records the agreed software services and constraints, including user-level and detailed system requirements. Study-guide sections

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Correct answer: A — Coding

Coding can be part of building an executable prototype even if the process diagram labels that work construction. It is therefore the offered activity that is not a separately named stage in the stated convention. Quick design, refinement and production engineering are named stages there. This answer concerns the diagram’s labels and does not claim that prototyping excludes coding or always follows one universal phase taxonomy.

Evidence in the complete study note

A prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility. A throwaway prototype is discarded after learning; an evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. A quick prototype may omit robustness, security or architecture, so do not deploy it unchanged without evaluation. Coding may occur during prototyping even if a diagram labels that activity construction rather than coding.SE07

Choice by choice

A · correct — Coding can occur inside construction without a separate stage label.

B · incorrect — Prototype refinement is a named stage.

C · incorrect — Engineering the production product is a named stage.

D · incorrect — Quick design is a named stage.

Question 36

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Correct answer: C — The need for highly skilled developers and designers.

SE07 describes RAD as rapid construction using timeboxes, user participation and often reusable components, but requiring skilled designers and developers. That staffing prerequisite is the listed drawback. Reuse and customer feedback are useful features. A combines the genuine prerequisite with a benefit, so C states the drawback accurately without misclassifying reuse.

Evidence in the complete study note

RAD uses rapid construction, timeboxing, user participation and often reusable components; it requires available users and skilled designers/developers. Reuse-oriented development searches components, evaluates fit, may adjust requirements, designs around interfaces and builds missing parts. Product-line assets may include requirements, architecture, components and tests; all are potentially reusable.SE07

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — It bundles a genuine staffing drawback with component reuse, which is generally a benefit.

B · incorrect — Component reuse helps rapid construction and is not the drawback asked for.

C · correct — RAD depends on skilled designers and developers, which can constrain staffing and feasibility.

D · incorrect — Customer feedback supports learning and fit rather than being the stated RAD disadvantage.

SE34 · Quality assurance, verification and validation

Evidence in the complete study note

Quality assurance establishes and checks processes/standards; quality control evaluates work products. Quality of conformance means following the design/specification; a product can conform to a poor specification. SE39 · Test process, plans and defect reports

Study-guide references

SE39 · Test process, plans and defect reports

Correct answer: B — Incident reports are execution outputs, rather than the test plan itself.

SE39 places objectives, scope, resources, schedule, risks and entry/exit criteria in test planning. Incident reports document observed problems during execution and are normally outputs of that work. A test plan describes intended work; incident/defect reports are normally execution outputs. Anyone finding a fault should record it; testers often coordinate reporting, but it is not their exclusive permission. Configuration control makes the tested version reproducible.SE39

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: A — Experience-based testing.

SE36 explicitly classifies exploratory testing as experience based because learning, test design and execution occur together. It may use knowledge of specifications or internals, but black-box, white-box and grey-box describe different bases of test derivation. None of them replaces the defining experience-based classification asked for in this question.

Evidence in the complete study note

Black-box techniques derive cases from specified behavior; white-box techniques derive them from internal structure; grey-box uses partial internal knowledge. Regression testing checks for unintended effects after change; confirmation testing checks the particular defect repair. Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution and is experience based. Manual/automated describe execution support, not a compulsory black-/white-box classification.SE36

D · incorrect — Partial internal knowledge can help exploration, but it does not define the technique.

Question 42

When comparing internal subsystem-grouping criteria with an external user perspective, which option names the external perspective rather than an internal structural or responsibility criterion?

  • A. Coupling
  • B. System's functionality
  • C. Cohesion
  • D. Users thinking

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · Question 39

  • University of Gondar model exam · Question 39

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: D — Users thinking

Coupling measures dependencies across subsystem boundaries, cohesion measures relatedness within a subsystem, and functionality helps assign responsibilities. These are internal structural grouping criteria. A user’s perspective describes externally needed tasks and behavior, so it is the different kind of information requested. User workflows can still inform architecture; the distinction does not claim users have no influence on design or that internal boundaries should ignore their needs.

Evidence in the complete study note

Group closely related objects and functionality, minimize associations crossing boundaries, and isolate communication infrastructure where useful. User workflows inform decomposition but do not alone dictate the internal structure. Analysis describes domain needs; subsystem decomposition is principally a design result. Architecture documentation supports communication and records major decisions, not every source-level execution step.SE21
Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Coupling directly measures inter-subsystem dependency.

B · incorrect — Functionality guides internal responsibility grouping.

C · incorrect — Cohesion measures how well elements grouped inside a subsystem serve a related purpose.

D · correct — This names the external user perspective rather than an internal structural measure or responsibility criterion.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE02 · Lifecycle phases and model selection

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

Correct answer: C — Result of system analysis is a model that includes a subsystem decomposition

Analysis clarifies the domain and externally required behavior; system design chooses the solution architecture and subsystem responsibilities. Attributing subsystem decomposition to the principal analysis result therefore confuses these stages. Requirements elicitation establishes stakeholder needs and constraints before the internal solution is selected. The revised elicitation option avoids the stronger claim that only one user’s viewpoint matters, while retaining the intended external-needs versus internal-design distinction.

Evidence in the complete study note

Analysis clarifies the problem; system design chooses architecture; object/detail design specifies interfaces and algorithms; implementation writes code; testing evaluates behavior; deployment puts it into service.SE02
User workflows inform decomposition but do not alone dictate the internal structure. Analysis describes domain needs; subsystem decomposition is principally a design result.SE21
User requirements describe stakeholder needs at a useful high level; system requirements specify detailed services and constraints.SE08

B · incorrect — Design develops the solution structure and implementation-facing decisions.

D · incorrect — Elicitation establishes externally visible stakeholder needs and constraints before choosing internal design.

Study-guide references

SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

Correct answer: C — Forms normally identify boundary objects.

SE13 defines entity objects as domain information and gives ReportForm as a boundary mediating interaction. Thus forms normally suggest boundary objects rather than entity objects. Real-world things, domain activities represented as information and relevant stored data can suggest entity candidates; those are heuristics, not mechanical rules guaranteeing a class for every noun or activity.

Use nouns as candidate objects, possessive descriptions as candidate attributes, and verbs such as manages/reports-to as candidate associations. These are heuristics, not automatic parsing rules. CRC means Class, Responsibilities, Collaborators. A control per use case or participating actor can be a useful starting point, not a mandatory UML rule or fixed object lifetime.SE13
A UI form is normally boundary, not entity.SE13

Question 51

Which team organization shares development decisions among team members rather than centralizing technical coordination in a chief programmer?

  • A. Functional
  • B. Project
  • C. Democratic
  • D. Chief programmer

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 23

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

SE32 · Team organization, development and maturity

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE32 · Team organization, development and maturity

Correct answer: C — Democratic

Democratic teams share decisions, whereas chief-programmer teams centralize technical coordination. Functional and project organizations classify how people are grouped, not how authority is distributed. Asking about shared decision-making therefore makes democratic the unique answer. It does not require every individual to perform every lifecycle task; a democratic team can still divide work by expertise and responsibilities.

Evidence in the complete study note

Functional organizations group specialists by discipline; project organizations group people around projects. Functional specialization helps staffing and knowledge continuity but may create handoff barriers. Democratic teams share decisions; chief-programmer teams centralize technical coordination. These are different classification dimensions. Tuckman’s sequence is forming→storming→norming→performing→adjourning: orientation, conflict, norms, effective work and closure.SE32

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Functional organization groups specialists by discipline.

B · incorrect — Project organization groups people by project rather than defining shared authority.

C · correct — Democratic teams share decisions.

D · incorrect — Chief-programmer teams centralize technical coordination.

SE32 · Team organization, development and maturity

Study-guide references

SE32 · Team organization, development and maturity

Correct answer: A — Historical CMM Level 2: Repeatable.

SE32 explicitly assigns requirements management, software project planning, quality assurance and configuration management to historical Software CMM Level 2. Its name is Repeatable, rather than the later CMMI label Managed. The other named choices correspond to levels 1, 3 and 4 in this historical model, so A matches both practices and terminology.

Evidence in the complete study note

Historical Software CMM levels are 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing. Level2 establishes basic project discipline including requirements management, project planning, quality assurance and configuration management. These historical labels must not be silently replaced by modern CMMI terminology. A maturity model concerns process capability, not a guarantee that every product is defect free.SE32

B · incorrect — Initial is historical Level 1, before the repeatable project discipline specified here.

D · incorrect — Managed is historical Software CMM Level 4; modern CMMI terminology must not be substituted.

Evidence in the complete study note

Acceptance testing supports the customer/user’s acceptance decision against agreed needs and criteria. Alpha typically happens in a controlled developer setting with selected users; beta uses external users in their environments. None of these levels is universally the longest. Unit is a level, while white-box is a technique; a unit can be tested using black-box cases too.SE35

C · incorrect — A technique based on external behavior, not a component level. See PDF p. 148, 144.

D · correct — Tests isolated objects or subsystems and their functionality. See PDF p. 148, 144.

Question 56

Requirements and technical feasibility are unclear. The immediate goal is to build an exploratory version for user feedback and feasibility learning, then discard it rather than deliver it as production software. Which model best names that immediate activity?

  • A. Incremental model
  • B. Prototype model
  • C. Spiral model
  • D. Waterfall model

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 44

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: B — Prototype model

A throwaway prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility and is discarded after learning. That exactly matches the immediate purpose specified. Incremental delivery would provide usable production capability; spiral would organize broader commitments around risk-driven cycles and might use a prototype within them. Classical waterfall favors understood requirements and familiar technology. The specific learning-and-discard goal therefore identifies the prototype model.

Evidence in the complete study note

A prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility. A throwaway prototype is discarded after learning; an evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. A quick prototype may omit robustness, security or architecture, so do not deploy it unchanged without evaluation. Coding may occur during prototyping even if a diagram labels that activity construction rather than coding.SE07
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Incremental delivery targets usable capability rather than a discarded exploratory artifact.

B · correct — A throwaway prototype explores needs and feasibility before being discarded.

C · incorrect — Spiral may use a prototype, but names the broader risk-driven process.

D · incorrect — The stated uncertainty lacks classical waterfall’s stable, familiar conditions.

Question 63

______a software product is necessary to rectify the bugs observed while the system is in use.

  • A. Adaptive maintenance
  • B. Corrective maintenance
  • C. Perfective maintenance
  • D. Preventive maintenance

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam · 2015 · Question 118

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk.

Study-guide sections

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

Correct answer: B — Corrective maintenance

The purpose of the change determines the maintenance category. Corrective maintenance repairs faults observed during use. Adaptive maintenance handles environmental changes, perfective maintenance improves useful capability or performance, and preventive maintenance reduces future risk before a corresponding failure occurs. Because the scenario starts with observed bugs that need repair, corrective maintenance is the direct category rather than one of the other three motives.

Evidence in the complete study note

Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Adaptive maintenance responds to a changed environment.

B · correct — Corrective maintenance repairs observed defects.

C · incorrect — Perfective maintenance improves useful capability or performance.

D · incorrect — Preventive maintenance reduces future risk rather than primarily fixing the stated observed bugs.

Question 66

Which are supported modularization benefits? Select all that apply. Read D as a claim that modularization alone guarantees security.

  • A. Smaller components are difficult to maintain
  • B. Components with high cohesion can be re-used again
  • C. Program can be divided based on functional aspects
  • D. Modularization alone guarantees security.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 81

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answers (select all): B, C — Components with high cohesion can be re-used again; Program can be divided based on functional aspects

Cohesive components with clear interfaces can be reused, and functional decomposition divides responsibilities into manageable modules. Smaller modules can also improve understanding and maintenance, so A reverses the ordinary benefit. Security requires appropriate protection and boundary enforcement; simply dividing code into modules does not guarantee it. Thus B and C are supported structural benefits without the unconditional security promise.

Evidence in the complete study note

Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — This reverses the ordinary maintenance benefit of manageable cohesive modules.

B · correct — Cohesive components can be reused in suitable contexts.

C · correct — Functional decomposition separates related responsibilities into modules.

D · incorrect — Module boundaries alone do not guarantee security.

Correct answer: C — Precondition, main scenario, alternative scenarios

A use-case description includes entry conditions, the numbered normal flow and exceptional cases.

Evidence in the complete study note

Example: Submit Incident. Precondition: officer authenticated. 1 Officer supplies location and description. 2 System validates details. 3 System records the incident. 4 System returns its ID. Alternative 2a: location missing → report the problem and request correction; save nothing. Success postcondition: incident and ID persist; failure guarantee: no partial record. Question 73

Which maintenance risk can arise from poorly designed objects with complex or poorly separated responsibilities?

  • A. Easier maintenance
  • B. Objects may be understood as stand-alone entities
  • C. Objects are potentially reusable components
  • D. Poorly designed objects can be difficult to maintain.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 91

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Correct answer: D — Poorly designed objects can be difficult to maintain.

Encapsulation and reuse can ease maintenance when objects have clear responsibilities and interfaces. Poor object design can still be complex, so its objects may become difficult to maintain. That conditional risk is D. The other choices describe potential advantages of well-designed objects rather than disadvantages arising from the stated poor design. Object orientation alone does not guarantee either maintenance outcome.

Evidence in the complete study note

Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22
Procedural decomposition organizes functions; object oriented decomposition organizes objects with state and behavior. Either can use iterative or sequential development. OOP does not automatically shorten every project. Reuse, encapsulation and consistent models can reduce duplication and ease change; poor object design can still be complex. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects; event-driven programs react to events.SE01
Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Easier maintenance is a potential benefit, not this risk.

B · incorrect — Understanding encapsulated objects through their interfaces is a potential benefit.

C · incorrect — Potential reuse is an advantage of suitable design.

D · correct — Poorly designed complex objects can be difficult to maintain.
