Study-guide sections

SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

Correct answer: C — Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy.

The filled diamond at Car denotes composition: Car is the whole and Engine is its strongly owned part. Composition destroys parts that remain owned when the whole is destroyed. Because this model forbids detachment or transfer, the Engine’s lifetime cannot continue independently of its Car. Temporary use would be a dependency, and inheritance would use a hollow generalization triangle instead.

Evidence in the complete study note

Composition uses a filled diamond at the whole end and strong ownership: a part is in at most one composite at a time, and parts still owned are destroyed with that composite. Parts may be detached/transferred under a defined model. Thus “cannot ever exist independently” is an oversimplification. For Car composing Engine, the diamond belongs beside Car; saying it points to Engine is imprecise. The Car–Engine example describes composition.SE18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Temporary use is a dependency, not composition.

B · incorrect — The stipulated permanent ownership excludes an independent Engine lifetime.

C · correct — Engine is the owned part and cannot outlive Car under the stated policy.

D · incorrect — Inheritance uses a hollow triangle rather than a filled diamond.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

Correct answer: C — . Not suitable for projects where requirements are at a moderate to high risk of changing

Waterfall requires early stable requirements and has difficulty responding to change, so moderate-to-high change risk is its documented disadvantage.

Evidence in the complete study note

Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03

Question 76

Which statement specifically constrains response-time performance under a stated workload?

  • A. The system allow user to generate PDF report.
  • B. The system respond to user's request within 2 second under normal load
  • C. . The system allow user to store data on relational database
  • D. The system allow user to submit emergency report

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 61

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Correct answer: B — The system respond to user's request within 2 second under normal load

The two-second response obligation bounds the speed of a service under the stated load, so it is a performance requirement. Generating a PDF and submitting an emergency report describe services the system provides. The database clause describes storage behavior together with an implementation choice; it does not impose a response-time threshold. The explicit performance scope removes the broader taxonomy overlap between nonfunctional requirements and technology constraints.

Evidence in the complete study note

Nonfunctional requirements include quality attributes and constraints. Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning. Security concerns protection; compatibility concerns cooperating environments; portability concerns moving environments; maintainability/supportability concern change, diagnosis and evolution.SE10
“Search responds within two seconds under 100 concurrent users” is measurable performance. “New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability. “Use Java” is a technology/pseudo-requirement, often separately classified as a system constraint. Dependability includes reliability, safety and robustness; portability is not its usual central category. Performance degradation at peak load primarily concerns performance, not automatically reliability.SE10

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Report generation specifies a service, not its response-time limit.

B · correct — A two-second response bound under normal load is a quantitative speed target.

C · incorrect — This specifies storage behavior and a database technology, without a timing bound.

D · incorrect — Submitting an emergency report specifies a function rather than its speed.

Question 80

Which choice most completely lists candidate heuristics for grouping objects into subsystems? Treat them as starting guidance, not mandatory boundaries.

  • A. Assign objects identified in one use case into the same subsystem.
  • B. Create a dedicated subsystem for objects used for moving data among subsystems.
  • C. Minimize the number of associations crossing subsystem boundaries.
  • D. All of the above

  • Computer Science model exam 2 · Question 18

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

Correct answer: D — All of the above

SE21 recommends grouping related functionality, minimizing cross-subsystem associations and isolating communication infrastructure where useful. Grouping objects serving one use case can be a starting heuristic, though workflows do not dictate every boundary. B and C directly support isolation and low coupling. Since the question asks what can be a heuristic, the inclusive option is appropriate.

Evidence in the complete study note

System design turns the analysis model into architecture: design goals, subsystem responsibilities, dependencies, hardware mapping, data management, access control, control flow and startup/shutdown/error policies. Detail/object design refines APIs, parameter/return types, exceptions, component choices and algorithms. A subsystem is a manageable logical collection with services and an interface; it need not be a physical replaceable artifact.SE21
Group closely related objects and functionality, minimize associations crossing boundaries, and isolate communication infrastructure where useful.SE21

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Objects collaborating on one use case can be grouped as a starting heuristic, subject to other design constraints.

B · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Communication infrastructure can be isolated in a dedicated subsystem when useful.

C · incorrect — True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Reducing cross-boundary associations reduces coupling between subsystems.

D · correct — All three can guide decomposition, provided use-case grouping is not treated as an absolute rule.

Study-guide sections

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

Correct answer: A — A physical and replaceable part of the system.

A subsystem is a manageable logical collection of responsibilities with services and an interface. It need not be a physical replaceable artifact, so A is false as a definition. Decomposing the designed solution into simpler groups helps manage complexity, and defined interfaces can encapsulate implementation state and behavior. These design benefits concern the solution organization rather than reducing the inherent complexity of its problem domain.

Evidence in the complete study note

Group closely related objects and functionality, minimize associations crossing boundaries, and isolate communication infrastructure where useful. User workflows inform decomposition but do not alone dictate the internal structure. Analysis describes domain needs; subsystem decomposition is principally a design result. Architecture documentation supports communication and records major decisions, not every source-level execution step.SE21
A subsystem is a manageable logical collection with services and an interface; it need not be a physical replaceable artifact.SE21

A · correct — A logical subsystem need not be physical or independently replaceable.

B · incorrect — Managing solution-design complexity is a supported decomposition benefit.

Question 82

Study-guide sections

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

SE-S07 · Scalability and robustness are different qualities

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

SE-S07 · Scalability and robustness are different qualities

Correct answer: A — A new user shall complete the main interface task within one minute without help.

A usability requirement states an observable target for successful and learnable use. Requiring a new user to finish a main interface task without help within one minute gives a task, user context, success condition and threshold. Robustness concerns dependable behavior under adverse conditions, mean time to failure is a reliability measure, and adaptability concerns change. Merely naming a user interface would not itself specify an obligation, so the option supplies a genuine requirement.

Evidence in the complete study note

Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning.SE10
“New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability.SE10
Robustness concerns reliable operation across varied or difficult operating conditions and controlled failure outside the supported range. It is different from usability, which concerns people successfully learning and carrying out tasks. Improving an interface’s task success does not by itself establish robustness under adverse conditions.SE-S07

Choice by choice

A · correct — The task-success and unaided-learning target is a measurable usability obligation.

B · incorrect — Robustness concerns dependable behavior under adverse conditions rather than ease of learning a task.

C · incorrect — Mean time to failure measures reliability rather than user task ease.

D · incorrect — Adaptability concerns accommodating change rather than the stated user task target.

Question 84

Which of the following is false about functional requirement?

  • A. Requirements should complete
  • B. Requirement should be accurate as possible.
  • C. Each requirement should state a clear, independently verifiable obligation.
  • D. A requirement can be interpreted in many exclusive ways.

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

Correct answer: D — A requirement can be interpreted in many exclusive ways.

Requirements should accurately reflect stakeholder needs, cover the agreed scope and express clear, verifiable obligations. Unambiguity requires one intended interpretation; mutually exclusive readings violate that property. The revised third option states the useful single-obligation writing rule without claiming that duplicate requirements can never be consolidated. Thus the multiple-interpretation option is the single false quality claim, while completeness, accuracy and clarity remain valid goals.

Evidence in the complete study note

Correct requirements reflect actual stakeholder needs. Complete requirements address the agreed scope, normal and exceptional behavior. Consistency excludes contradictions. Clarity/unambiguity gives one intended interpretation; feasibility/realism means achievable within constraints. Verifiability means objective evidence can check fulfillment. Replace “fast for most users” with a defined metric, workload and threshold.SE11
Write one clear obligation with an actor/trigger, action and observable result.SE09

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Completeness requires coverage of the agreed behavior and exceptional cases.

B · incorrect — Accuracy requires requirements to reflect the actual stakeholder needs.

C · incorrect — A clear independently verifiable obligation supports precise specification.

D · correct — Mutually exclusive readings violate the unambiguity requirement.

Question 86

Which named approach develops an experimental version specifically to explore unclear requirements or feasibility, and can therefore serve both as a development approach and an elicitation technique?

  • A. Spiral process model
  • B. Waterfall process model
  • C. Prototype process model
  • D. Agile process model

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: C — Prototype process model

Prototyping uses an early experimental representation or working version to discover requirements, usability needs or technical feasibility. It can be organized as a development approach and also used within elicitation. Spiral may contain a prototype to reduce risk, but risk-driven cycles define spiral itself. Waterfall names phased development, while Agile names a broader adaptive approach. The question asks the named experimentation technique that directly serves both purposes.

Evidence in the complete study note

A prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility. A throwaway prototype is discarded after learning; an evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. A quick prototype may omit robustness, security or architecture, so do not deploy it unchanged without evaluation. Coding may occur during prototyping even if a diagram labels that activity construction rather than coding.SE07
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Spiral may employ prototypes but is itself defined by risk-driven cycles.

B · incorrect — Waterfall is a phased lifecycle rather than the experimentation technique described.

C · correct — Prototyping directly explores requirements or feasibility using an experimental version.

D · incorrect — Agile is a broad adaptive approach and can use several elicitation techniques.

Functional testing tests requirements from the RAD and, if available, the user manual. Of the options, the requirements specification is the primary basis; the user manual is supplementary.

Study-guide sections

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: D — None of statements A–C is false.

Low coupling limits dependencies between subsystems, while high cohesion keeps related responsibilities together inside each subsystem. The first statement recommends this combination, the second identifies cohesion within the subsystem, and the third identifies coupling across subsystems. All three substantive statements are therefore true. The final alternative is explicitly the response for finding no false statement among those three, rather than a self-referential assertion about all choices.

Evidence in the complete study note

Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Low coupling and high cohesion are the stated decomposition goals.

B · incorrect — Cohesion concerns relatedness and dependencies among elements within a subsystem.

C · incorrect — Coupling concerns dependencies between subsystems.

D · correct — None of the substantive statements A–C is false, so this is the required response.

A software design model states exact withdraw preconditions and balance equations but omits physical implementation detail. Compare it with an informal mathematical sketch that leaves those constraints unspecified and a fully detailed engine drawing. Which statement is FALSE for these particular models?

  • A. This software model is less precise than the specified mathematical sketch.
  • B. This software model is more abstract than the fully detailed engine drawing.
  • C. A main role of this model is to represent the software designer’s ideas.
  • D. None of A–C is false.

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 3 · Question 26

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Correct answer: A — This software model is less precise than the specified mathematical sketch.

The software model states exact preconditions and balance equations, whereas the informal mathematical sketch omits those constraints. It is therefore not less precise in the stated comparison, making A false. Omitting implementation detail makes it more abstract than the specified detailed engine drawing, and representing design ideas remains a legitimate purpose. These are scenario-specific judgments rather than universal rankings of all software and mathematical models.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose designs by their effect on stated goals. Fine-grained self-contained components, separation of producers/consumers and limited shared mutable data often improve maintainability. Trade-offs remain: interfaces can add latency, isolation can complicate transactions, and global state can simplify one operation while coupling many others. Prefer measurable quality scenarios to counting components alone.SE43
A contract states preconditions, postconditions and invariants. For withdraw(amount): require amount>0 and amount<=balance; ensure balance=oldBalance-amount; preserve balance>=0. Validation checks inputs; implementation enforces the transition. A complete feature needs both UI/API and persisted behavior, not only a diagram.SE25
A layer is a logical abstraction level; a tier is a deployment separation. A closed layered architecture permits calls only to the immediately lower layer; an open one permits approved skipping. For top-to-bottom A,B,C,D, A→B obeys closed layering, A→C skips, and lower-to-upper calls violate the simple dependency rule unless explicitly mediated by a defined mechanism.SE23
A structure is the elements/relations themselves; a view represents selected aspects.SE23

Choice by choice

A · correct — Its exact constraints make the stated less-precise comparison false.

B · incorrect — The software model omits implementation detail retained in the detailed drawing.

C · incorrect — A design model can represent the designer’s ideas and decisions.

D · incorrect — A is false, so the no-false-statements alternative is wrong.

Study-guide references

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

SE-S03 · Modeling categories and data diagrams

Correct answer: B — Data-flow diagrams.

SE20 defines a DFD through data flows, stores and transformations from inputs to outputs. That matches the functional-transformation focus in the stem. An ER diagram focuses on domain data relationships, while a component diagram describes software components and dependencies. A DFD need not show detailed control timing merely because it depicts connected transformations.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose a sequence diagram for message order between participants, a state machine for event-dependent state changes, and activity for workflow. Both sequence and state diagrams describe behavior over time. State machines are useful for objects with significant states, whether entity or control. A DFD shows data stores/flows and transformations from inputs to outputs; it is not a UML diagram.SE20
An entity–relationship diagram models entity types, their attributes and the relationships between them, commonly for data design. Its focus differs from a use-case diagram of external roles and goals, a class diagram of classes and their features, or a deployment diagram mapping artifacts to execution nodes.SE-S03

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — ER diagrams describe entities and relationships rather than transformations of input data into outputs.

B · correct — DFDs depict data flows and the processes that transform inputs into outputs.

C · incorrect — Component diagrams describe component interfaces and dependencies rather than this data-transformation view.

D · incorrect — DFD is listed and directly matches the functional-transformation description.

Question 93

Which choice gives the most complete supported comparison of object-oriented model continuity and transitions between different development models?

  • A. Object-oriented development can use a consistent vocabulary of objects and classes across analysis and design.
  • B. Reuse and consistent models in object-oriented development can reduce development effort and duration on suitable projects.
  • C. Moving between different representations in a traditional phased approach can add translation complexity and errors.
  • D. All statements A–C are correct.

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 3 · Question 29

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

Correct answer: D — All statements A–C are correct.

A consistent object vocabulary across development stages can reduce errors from translating between unrelated models. Reuse and continuity can also reduce effort on suitable projects, while transitions between different representations can add complexity. These are potential benefits and risks, not guarantees that every OO project is shorter or every traditional project is worse. With those qualifications, all three substantive statements are supported, making their aggregate the most complete answer.

Evidence in the complete study note

Software engineering applies systematic methods to development, operation and maintenance. A software product includes executable code and relevant requirements, designs, test assets, configuration and user documentation. A process defines activities, ordering, roles, products and entry/exit conditions. Its four broad activities are specification, design/implementation, validation and evolution.SE01
Procedural decomposition organizes functions; object oriented decomposition organizes objects with state and behavior. Either can use iterative or sequential development. OOP does not automatically shorten every project. Reuse, encapsulation and consistent models can reduce duplication and ease change; poor object design can still be complex. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects; event-driven programs react to events.SE01
An object-oriented approach can use a consistent vocabulary of objects, classes and relationships across analysis, design and implementation. Models are refined for different purposes rather than being identical artifacts. This continuity can reduce translation errors and effort; reusable classes can shorten suitable projects, but neither shorter duration nor good design is guaranteed.SE-S02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — True but incomplete alone: a consistent object/class vocabulary can connect analysis and design.

B · incorrect — True but incomplete alone: reuse and model continuity can reduce effort, without guaranteeing it.

C · incorrect — True but incomplete alone: translation between different representations can add complexity or errors.

D · correct — All three qualified statements hold, so the aggregate is the complete selection.

Question 96

A takes 5 days. B takes 3 days and C takes 4 days; both depend only on A and may run in parallel with sufficient resources. The project finishes when all three complete. What is its earliest duration?

  • A. 3 days
  • B. 4 days
  • C. 5 days
  • D. 9 days

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 3 · Question 32

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Correct answer: D — 9 days

A completes at day five. B and C then start together, finishing at days eight and nine respectively. The project must wait for both required tasks, so its earliest finish is 5+max(3,4)=9 days. Adding all durations would ignore the permitted parallelism, while using eight days would count only the shorter A–B path and leave C incomplete.

Evidence in the complete study note

If A takes 5 days and B=3,C=4 both follow A, project duration is 5+max(3,4)=9 days. B finishes at 8, but the project waits for C at 9. If paths B5+C6 and D8+E3 share a zero-duration start/end, both total 11; there are two critical paths, not one.SE29

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Three counts B alone and omits its predecessor.

B · incorrect — Four counts C alone and omits A.

C · incorrect — Five stops after A, before both successors.

D · correct — A followed by the longer parallel branch takes nine days.

Question 97

A project starts at day 0 and must finish at day 9. It consists of exactly two parallel paths, A → B and C → D. A and C have no predecessors, B depends only on A, D depends only on C, and the project finishes when both B and D are complete. Activity durations and early times are: A: duration 4 days, ES=0, EF=4; B: duration 5 days, ES=4, EF=9; C: duration 3 days, ES=0, EF=3; D: duration 6 days, ES=3, EF=9. What is the total slack (float) of Activity C?

  • A. 0 days
  • B. 1 day
  • C. 3 days
  • D. 6 days

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 3 · Question 33

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Correct answer: A — 0 days.

Each complete path takes 9 days: A→B is 4+5 and C→D is 3+6. Working backward from day 9, D must start by day 3. Therefore C must finish by day 3 and start by day 0. C has LS=0 and ES=0, so total slack = LS−ES = 0 days (equivalently LF−EF = 3−3). A is correct. Delaying C would delay its successor D and the required project finish.

Evidence in the complete study note

Early start/finish values alone do not determine slack without successor relationships and the project completion constraint. If C3→D6 is a complete path parallel to A4→B5 and both finish at day9, C has zero float. That network cannot be silently inferred from four unrelated ES/EF rows.SE30
Traditional CPM uses point durations; PERT models uncertainty with optimistic a, most-likely m and pessimistic b. The classic estimate is TE=(a+4m+b)/6 and variance=((b-a)/6)^2. For 3,6,15 days, TE=42/6=7 days and variance=4 days². Do not replace the weighted estimate by a simple average. These formulas are approximations, not guaranteed actual completion times.SE30

Choice by choice

A · correct — C has latest start 0 and earliest start 0, giving zero total slack.

B · incorrect — A one-day delay would make the C→D path finish on day 10, beyond the day-9 finish.

C · incorrect — C’s three-day duration is not its slack; a three-day delay would finish this path on day 12.

D · incorrect — D’s six-day duration is not C’s slack; a six-day delay to C would finish the path on day 15.

What defining intention distinguishes a throwaway prototype from an evolutionary prototype?

  • B. It involves just one task

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE07 · Prototypes, RAD and reuse-oriented development

Correct answer: D — It is intended to be discarded after learning, rather than refined into the production system.

A throwaway prototype is built to learn about requirements, usability or feasibility and is discarded after serving that purpose. An evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. Either may involve successive steps, multiple tasks and varying development time, so those features do not define the difference. The artifact’s intended future, rather than how quickly it was built, distinguishes the approaches.

Evidence in the complete study note

A prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility. A throwaway prototype is discarded after learning; an evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. A quick prototype may omit robustness, security or architecture, so do not deploy it unchanged without evaluation. Coding may occur during prototyping even if a diagram labels that activity construction rather than coding.SE07

B · incorrect — Either kind can explore more than one task.

Question 101

Which factors can cause requirements, scope or priorities to evolve during a project? Select all that apply.

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — Changing needs of stakeholders; Advances in technology; Market dynamics; Lack of project funding

Stakeholder needs can change the services required, technology can introduce new constraints or opportunities, and market dynamics can alter business priorities. A funding shortfall can also reduce scope or force reprioritization. The note explicitly includes all four sources of change. Their effects depend on the project, but each can cause evolution, so none is an unconditional exception.

Evidence in the complete study note

Trace each requirement backward to its source/rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Record dependencies among requirements. A traceability matrix links these artifacts and helps impact analysis; it is not just a cost/schedule ledger. Stakeholders must negotiate conflicting requirements rather than independently approving incompatible demands. Scope, understanding and volatility are distinct elicitation difficulties.SE11
Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40
Markets, technology, stakeholders and funding can all change scope or priorities.SE40

Question 102

Study-guide sections

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: C — Regression testing.

The concern is that small changes may disturb other previously working parts of the software. Regression testing means checking unintended effects after change, rather than only confirming the defect. Such testing can span multiple levels and a large scope; the question describes its purpose, not the size of a unit or an acceptance decision.

Evidence in the complete study note

Black-box techniques derive cases from specified behavior; white-box techniques derive them from internal structure; grey-box uses partial internal knowledge. Regression testing checks for unintended effects after change; confirmation testing checks the particular defect repair. Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution and is experience based. Manual/automated describe execution support, not a compulsory black-/white-box classification.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Preventive testing is not the defined technique for detecting unintended effects of a specific software change.

B · incorrect — Unit testing isolates a small component and does not by itself define the cross-system change-impact purpose.

C · correct — Regression tests check whether changes unintentionally damage previously working behavior elsewhere.

D · incorrect — Acceptance testing supports a user acceptance decision rather than specifically checking unintended change effects.

SE37 · Equivalence, boundaries and decision tables

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE37 · Equivalence, boundaries and decision tables

Correct answer: B — Black-box, specification-based testing.

SE37 derives decision-table cases from combinations of specified conditions and resulting actions. This is specification-based rather than code-structure-based testing. It therefore belongs to black-box techniques. Experience or partial internal knowledge may help a tester, but they do not define the decision-table method or change its condition/action test basis.

Evidence in the complete study note

A decision table lists condition combinations and resulting actions. For validCard and enoughFunds, enumerate TT,TF,FT,FF; specify dispense only for TT and the proper rejection for others. Cover feasible rules rather than blindly using every impossible combination. These are specification-based techniques. Test requirements can also define state-transition cases, such as rejecting dispatch from an already closed incident.SE37

B · correct — Decision tables derive cases from specified conditions and expected actions, making them black-box.

D · incorrect — Partial knowledge of internals is not required to derive decision-table test cases.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: B — Modularization

Separating unrelated responsibilities into cohesive components is modularization: the design is divided into modules with focused purposes. Refactoring can describe behavior-preserving restructuring of an existing solution, but that broader activity is not the specific decomposition concept requested. Information hiding concerns concealed decisions behind interfaces, while refinement is a general elaboration concept. The stated split primarily establishes better module responsibility boundaries.

Evidence in the complete study note

Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Correct answer: C — Bottom up

Bottom-up design begins with existing components and assembles them into a larger solution. Top-down design instead starts with high-level structure and refines it, although it can still reuse components later. A hybrid combines the two directions, but the question asks which approach characteristically begins with the parts. Reuse by itself would not distinguish them; the explicit starting direction does.

Evidence in the complete study note

Use abstraction and decomposition to manage complexity; preserve consistency, traceability and clear responsibilities. Top-down design refines high-level structure; bottom-up design assembles existing components. A hybrid combines both. SOLID includes Single Responsibility, Open–Closed, Liskov substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion. Depend on abstractions; add compatible extensions; avoid forcing unused operations. DRY limits duplicated knowledge, KISS avoids unnecessary complexity, and YAGNI avoids speculative work.SE25

SE34 · Quality assurance, verification and validation

Verification checks whether specified functions and obligations have been implemented correctly. Validation checks whether the built product meets intended stakeholder needs. Both can use reviews, analysis or execution, so “human-only versus computer-only” is false.SE34

Question 111

A project manager is using PERT to estimate the duration of a project activity. The optimistic time (a) is 3 days, the most likely time (m) is 6 days, and the pessimistic time (b) is 15 days. What is the expected time (TE) for the activity?

  • A. 8 days
  • B. 10 days
  • C. 7 days
  • D. 9 days

Source

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 31

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE30 · Slack assumptions and PERT calculations

Correct answer: C — 7 days.

Use TE=(a+4m+b)/6 from SE30 with a=3, m=6 and b=15. The numerator is 3+24+15=42, so TE=42/6=7 days. A simple average would give 8, but that discards the fourfold weighting of the most-likely estimate. The expected duration is an estimate, not a guaranteed actual completion time.

Evidence in the complete study note

Traditional CPM uses point durations; PERT models uncertainty with optimistic a, most-likely m and pessimistic b. The classic estimate is TE=(a+4m+b)/6 and variance=((b-a)/6)^2. For 3,6,15 days, TE=42/6=7 days and variance=4 days². Do not replace the weighted estimate by a simple average. These formulas are approximations, not guaranteed actual completion times.SE30

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Eight is the simple mean of 3, 6 and 15, not the weighted PERT estimate.

B · incorrect — Ten does not result from substituting the three given values into the PERT formula.

C · correct — The weighted sum is 42 and dividing by six gives 7 days.

D · incorrect — Nine does not equal the PERT weighted expected time for these estimates.

Question 112

Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a critical path in a CPM network diagram for software development?

  • A. Any delay in tasks on this path delays the entire project.
  • B. It identifies tasks with strict dependencies.
  • C. It represents the longest sequence of tasks.
  • D. It has the most slack (buffer time) compared to other paths.

Source

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 32

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Correct answer: D — It has the most slack (buffer time) compared to other paths.

The critical path is the chain determining project duration. The maximum-slack claim contradicts this: freely postponable tasks would not determine the earliest completion under a fixed network.

Evidence in the complete study note

In a dependency network, ES=max predecessor EF and EF=ES+duration; start tasks have ES=0 unless another constraint applies. Project earliest finish is the maximum terminal EF. Backward, LF=min successor LS and LS=LF-duration, starting from the required finish. Total float/slack=LS-ES=LF-EF. A critical path has the longest total duration and normally zero float in an unconstrained schedule.SE29

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Delaying a controlling chain delays completion. See PDF p. 95.

B · incorrect — Dependency order constrains the chain, though noncritical tasks can also have strict dependencies. See PDF p. 95.

C · incorrect — The duration-determining chain is the longest required chain in the fixed-duration network. See PDF p. 95.

D · correct — Maximum slack is inconsistent with a path that controls completion; no resource constraints are assumed. See PDF p. 95.

Question 113

A zero-duration start A leads to parallel paths B(5)→C(6) and D(8)→E(3), both ending at a zero-duration finish. Which critical-path statements are true? Select all that apply. Multiple critical paths are allowed.

  • A. A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 11 days.
  • B. A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 11 days.
  • C. A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 14 days.
  • D. A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 14 days.

Adapted from

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 33

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.

Study-guide sections

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE29 · Critical path: forward and backward passes

Correct answers (select all): A, B — A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 11 days.; A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 11 days.

The B–C branch totals 5+6=11 days and the D–E branch totals 8+3=11 days. With zero-duration start and finish, both are equally longest complete paths, so both are critical and the project duration is eleven days. There is no rule requiring a unique critical path. The alternatives using fourteen days miscalculate the corresponding branch totals.

Evidence in the complete study note

In a dependency network, ES=max predecessor EF and EF=ES+duration; start tasks have ES=0 unless another constraint applies. Project earliest finish is the maximum terminal EF. Backward, LF=min successor LS and LS=LF-duration, starting from the required finish. Total float/slack=LS-ES=LF-EF. A critical path has the longest total duration and normally zero float in an unconstrained schedule.SE29
If A takes 5 days and B=3,C=4 both follow A, project duration is 5+max(3,4)=9 days. B finishes at 8, but the project waits for C at 9. If paths B5+C6 and D8+E3 share a zero-duration start/end, both total 11; there are two critical paths, not one.SE29

Choice by choice

A · correct — The B–C branch totals eleven and is critical.

B · correct — The D–E branch also totals eleven and is critical.

C · incorrect — Eight plus three is eleven, not fourteen.

D · incorrect — Five plus six is eleven, not fourteen.

Question 116

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Correct answer: C — Trace each requirement back to its source and rationale.

SE11 directs requirements backward to their source or rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Backward traceability therefore establishes why a requirement exists and where it came from. It can assist reviews, but redundancy detection is not its definition. Design mappings and future phases primarily describe the forward direction.

Evidence in the complete study note

Trace each requirement backward to its source/rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Record dependencies among requirements. D · incorrect — Links toward later project artifacts describe forward rather than backward traceability.

Question 120

First design the very high level structure of the system. Then gradually work down to detailed decisions about low-level constructs. Which design approach follows the given strategy?

  • B. System design
  • C. Top-down
  • D. Hybrid

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Study-guide sections

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Correct answer: C — Top-down design.

The described direction starts with high-level structure and refines it into lower-level decisions. SE25 explicitly calls that top-down design. Bottom-up starts from existing components and assembles them; a hybrid combines directions. System design names a design activity or level, not the specific refinement direction requested by the question.

Evidence in the complete study note

Use abstraction and decomposition to manage complexity; preserve consistency, traceability and clear responsibilities. Top-down design refines high-level structure; bottom-up design assembles existing components. A hybrid combines both. SOLID includes Single Responsibility, Open–Closed, Liskov substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion. Depend on abstractions; add compatible extensions; avoid forcing unused operations. DRY limits duplicated knowledge, KISS avoids unnecessary complexity, and YAGNI avoids speculative work.SE25

D · incorrect — A hybrid combines both directions; the stem describes only top-down refinement.

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: B — When major risks make one-block development unsafe.

SE06 uses explicit risk assessment and reduction to distinguish spiral development from other iterative approaches. B directly states that risk makes a single overall commitment inappropriate. Changing or unstable requirements can occur in several processes and do not alone identify spiral; clear business modeling likewise does not supply the distinctive risk-based reason.

Evidence in the complete study note

Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06
Use risk emphasis to distinguish spiral from a generic changing-requirements scenario.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Understanding business modeling alone does not identify the need for risk-driven spiral cycles.

B · correct — Important risks justify staged investigation and commitment rather than building the entire system in one block.

C · incorrect — Possible requirement changes fit multiple processes and omit spiral's distinguishing explicit risk emphasis.

D · incorrect — Unstable requirements alone do not uniquely select spiral over other adaptive approaches.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: D — The module groups similar-category operations.

SE22 defines logical cohesion as grouping operations in a similar category, often selected through a flag. D matches that shared logical category. A instead describes temporal cohesion, where operations occur at the same time. Interface complexity concerns dependencies, and a loose collection of unrelated tasks does not state the defining category-based relationship.

Evidence in the complete study note

Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

D · correct — Grouping similar-category operations is the defining feature of logical cohesion.

Question 137

If the estimate for total discounted benefits for a project is Birr 120,000 and total discounted cost is Birr 100,000, what is the estimated return on investment (ROI) percentage?

  • B. 12%
  • C. 10%
  • D. 20%

Study-guide sections

SE31 · Business value, risks and resource optimization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE31 · Business value, risks and resource optimization

Correct answer: D — 20%.

The benefits and costs are already discounted to a common date, so use SE31 directly: ROI=(120000−100000)/100000×100%. Net benefit is Birr 20000, and dividing by Birr 100000 gives 0.20, or 20%. Dividing total benefits by costs would report a benefit-cost ratio, not the net return percentage requested.

Evidence in the complete study note

With benefits and costs already discounted to a common date, ROI=(benefits-costs)/costs*100%. Birr120000 benefits and Birr100000 costs give 20%, not 120%. Identify project risks to resources/schedule, product risks to quality, and business risks to the organization. Analyze likelihood and impact, plan responses and monitor.SE31

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — Twelve percent is not 20000 divided by 100000 as a percentage.

C · incorrect — Ten percent understates the calculated net return of twenty percent.

D · correct — Net benefit is Birr 20000, which is 20% of the Birr 100000 cost.

Question 138

In a closed layered architecture with A,B,C,D from top to bottom, a pair (X,Y) means X directly calls Y. Calls may go only to the immediately lower layer. Which pair obeys this policy?

  • A. (A,C)
  • B. (D,A)
  • C. (A,B)
  • D. (C,B)

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 21

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

Correct answer: C — (A,B)

Closed layering permits a layer to call only the immediately lower layer. A→B follows that adjacency and direction, so C is valid. A→C skips B and violates the closed policy even though it would be possible in a suitably open architecture. D→A and C→B point upward, which the stipulated dependency policy also forbids. The ordered pair is interpreted as caller then callee.

Evidence in the complete study note

A layer is a logical abstraction level; a tier is a deployment separation. A closed layered architecture permits calls only to the immediately lower layer; an open one permits approved skipping. For top-to-bottom A,B,C,D, A→B obeys closed layering, A→C skips, and lower-to-upper calls violate the simple dependency rule unless explicitly mediated by a defined mechanism.SE23

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — A→C skips B.

B · incorrect — D→A points upward.

C · correct — A→B calls the immediately lower layer.

D · incorrect — C→B points upward.

SE39 · Test process, plans and defect reports

Correct answers (select all): A, B, C, D — Tester; Requirement engineer; Developer; Scrum master

Anyone discovering a fault should record it with enough evidence to reproduce and assess it. Testers often coordinate reporting, but requirements engineers, developers and Scrum masters should also document faults they discover. The report should identify the relevant environment, steps and expected versus actual behavior. Therefore all four roles meet the stated discoverer-based responsibility rather than only the dedicated tester.

Plan objectives, scope, resources, schedule, risks and entry/exit criteria. Analyze the test basis for testable features and defects; design cases/expected results; implement data, scripts and environment; execute and compare; report defects; evaluate completion. Analysis asks what to test and assesses testability; design asks how. Monitoring/control run across these activities.SE39
Anyone finding a fault should record it; testers often coordinate reporting, but it is not their exclusive permission.SE39

Question 141

Which statement accurately describes the main evidential goal of software testing within quality assurance?

  • A. To achieve project timelines and deadlines.
  • B. To monitor the entire SDLC.
  • C. To generate software requirement and design documentation.

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 42

Study-guide sections

SE34 · Quality assurance, verification and validation

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE34 · Quality assurance, verification and validation

Correct answer: D — To assess conformance to specified requirements, reveal defects and increase confidence through evidence.

Testing evaluates behavior against required results, revealing failures and increasing confidence in conformance. It does not generally guarantee correctness over every possible input or environment. Meeting schedules and monitoring the whole lifecycle are broader management or assurance activities, while requirements and design documentation usually form part of the test basis. Option D states the supported evidential purpose without promising certainty.

Evidence in the complete study note

Quality assurance establishes and checks processes/standards; quality control evaluates work products. An SQA plan identifies standards, responsibilities, evaluations, reviews, audits and assurance records. Quality of conformance means following the design/specification; a product can conform to a poor specification. Verification asks whether specified obligations are implemented correctly; validation asks whether the product meets intended stakeholder needs. Both can use reviews, analysis or execution, so “human-only versus computer-only” is false.SE34
Tests increase confidence and reveal defects but cannot generally guarantee correctness over every possible input.SE34

Which question is outside the architectural abstraction level and instead asks for every source-level execution detail?

  • A. Which architectural organization is best for delivering the functional requirements?
  • B. How the system will be distributed across a number of cores or processors
  • C. Which variable is assigned at every individual source-code execution step?

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

SE21 · Design and subsystem decomposition

Correct answer: C — Which variable is assigned at every individual source-code execution step?

Architecture addresses major organization, responsibilities, allocation and style decisions. Selecting an arrangement for required behavior, mapping work to processors and choosing patterns are therefore valid architectural concerns. Enumerating every source-level assignment on every execution step is implementation-level tracing, beyond the abstraction of architecture documentation. Option C supplies that genuine exception while preserving the question’s comparison of architectural and detailed concerns.

Evidence in the complete study note

A structure is the elements/relations themselves; a view represents selected aspects. Module structures show code organization, component-and-connector structures runtime interaction, and allocation structures map software to hardware, teams or environment. Processes/threads belong in concurrency views. Evaluate architectures against quality attributes and scenarios; processor allocation, decomposition and style selection can all be architectural concerns.SE23
System design turns the analysis model into architecture: design goals, subsystem responsibilities, dependencies, hardware mapping, data management, access control, control flow and startup/shutdown/error policies. Detail/object design refines APIs, parameter/return types, exceptions, component choices and algorithms. A subsystem is a manageable logical collection with services and an interface; it need not be a physical replaceable artifact.SE21
Architecture documentation supports communication and records major decisions, not every source-level execution step.SE21

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Organization supporting required behavior is architectural.

B · incorrect — Processor allocation is an architectural concern.

C · correct — Every source-level execution step exceeds the architectural abstraction.

Study-guide references

SE38 · Statement, decision and branch coverage

Correct answer: A — Four tests for 100% decision coverage.

There are three decisions: width>length and one separate height comparison inside each outer branch. Covering both inner outcomes requires two tests with outer true and two with outer false. For example (w,l,h)=(3,2,4),(3,2,1),(2,3,4),(2,3,1) covers all outcomes. One execution cannot visit both outer branches, so two or three tests cannot suffice; six are unnecessary.

Evidence in the complete study note

Statement coverage is the number of distinct executable statements exercised divided by the total executable statements in the declared test scope. Unreachable statements can prevent100%; any justified exclusions must be documented with the adjusted scope. Decision coverage counts decision outcomes; branch coverage counts control-flow edges, including unconditional edges under the stated convention. Testing both true and false of each decision may need more than two overall test cases when branches nest. Coverage is evidence of exercised structure, not proof of all behavior.SE38
In the width/length/height program, the outer if has separate inner decisions in each branch. Need outer true with inner true and false, and outer false with its inner true and false: four tests, for example (w,l,h)=(3,2,4),(3,2,1),(2,3,4),(2,3,1). One run cannot exercise both outer branches. All paths may be infeasible or infinite with loops; specify the chosen coverage target.SE38

Choice by choice

A · correct — Four tests cover true/false of the inner decision on each of the two outer branches.

B · incorrect — Six can cover the decisions, but four suffice; it is not the required minimum.

C · incorrect — Two cover the outer decision but cannot cover both outcomes of both separate inner decisions.

D · incorrect — Three leave at least one inner decision outcome uncovered because each outer branch needs two tests.

  • B. Inagile life cycle the project scope is generally determined early in the project life cycle, but time and cost estimates are routinely modified

Study-guide sections

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Correct answers (select all): B, D — Inagile life cycle the project scope is generally determined early in the project life cycle, but time and cost estimates are routinely modified; Inagile life cycles, the project scope cannot be outlined and agreed before the start of iteration.

Classical waterfall establishes planned baselines early, and incremental work adds functionality in successive deliveries. Agile instead adapts content while its timeboxes tend to remain fixed, so B misstates the general organizing pattern. D is also false because Agile permits outlining and agreeing scope before an iteration; planning continues as evidence changes. Adaptation does not mean that scope discussion or early agreement is prohibited.

Evidence in the complete study note

Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Early planned baselines fit classical waterfall.

B · correct — The claim reverses the timeboxed/adaptive-content characterization.

C · incorrect — Successive additions of usable functionality fit incremental delivery.

D · correct — Agile permits scope discussion and agreement before an iteration.

Which design pattern is used to restore the state of an object to its previous state?

  • C. Momento pattern
  • D. Visitor pattern

Study-guide sections

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Correct answer: C — Memento, printed as Momento.

SE27 explicitly identifies Memento as storing and restoring state while hiding representation, and notes that Momento in this question bank is a spelling error for Memento. That makes C the intended pattern name. Iterator traverses a collection and Observer notifies subscribers; neither supplies the state-snapshot restoration responsibility asked for here.

Evidence in the complete study note

Factory Method lets subclasses choose a concrete product through a creation operation, reducing coupling to concrete constructors. A simple factory centralizes creation but is not identical to Factory Method. Singleton controls access to one instance; Observer notifies subscribers; Memento stores/restores state while hiding representation; Iterator traverses; Decorator adds behavior through wrapping. The pattern name is Memento, not Momento.SE27
Variability can use selectable features, omission/inclusion and extension points; overloading supplies alternate signatures in code but is not every variability mechanism. Testability improves with controllable inputs, observable outputs, replaceable dependencies and limited structural complexity. A sandbox can isolate execution. Assess each design claim independently before evaluating a combined statement.SE27

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Iterator traverses elements rather than storing a restorable snapshot of object state.

B · incorrect — Observer notifies subscribers about changes rather than restoring an earlier object state.

C · correct — Momento refers here to Memento, the state capture-and-restoration pattern.

D · incorrect — Visitor is not the state-snapshot restoration pattern; the note assigns that role to Memento.

Question 150

During which listed activity should the test plan define configuration-management procedures alongside objectives, resources and schedule, before those procedures are applied during execution?

  • B. During test planning
  • C. During test closing

SE33 · Configuration, change control and version control

SE39 · Test process, plans and defect reports

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE33 · Configuration, change control and version control

SE39 · Test process, plans and defect reports

Correct answer: B — During test planning

Test planning specifies intended work, objectives, resources and schedule; configuration-management procedures should be defined early as part of that preparation. They then apply throughout testing to preserve reproducible builds, data and environments. Execution and closing use those procedures rather than being their exclusive establishment point. Initiation may set context, but the question specifically asks for the activity that defines them in the test plan.

Evidence in the complete study note

Configuration management identifies controlled items, versions/baselines, change procedures, status and audits. Items may include source code, requirements, manuals, test plans, environments and build configurations. A team’s ordinary browser is usually a tool rather than product CI, but a controlled test-browser version may be an environment CI.SE33
A test plan describes intended work; incident/defect reports are normally execution outputs. A defect report should identify build/environment, steps, expected versus actual behavior, evidence and severity. Anyone finding a fault should record it; testers often coordinate reporting, but it is not their exclusive permission. Configuration control makes the tested version reproducible.SE39
Plan test configuration management early and apply it throughout testing, not at just one exclusive phase.SE33
Analysis asks what to test and assesses testability; design asks how.SE39

B · correct — Test planning defines procedures with the other planned work.

C · incorrect — Closing preserves final artifacts under established control.

Question 154

Which of the following UML element is wrongly applied?

  • A. Use case diagram represents an interaction with the system
  • B. Sequence diagram shows the sequence of interactions required to complete some operation
  • C. An activity diagram primarily specifies the persistent lifecycle states of one object and the event-triggered transitions between those states.
  • D. Class diagram shows the object classes in a system and their relation

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 69

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

SE17 · Class diagrams, visibility and multiplicity

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

SE17 · Class diagrams, visibility and multiplicity

Correct answer: C — An activity diagram primarily specifies the persistent lifecycle states of one object and the event-triggered transitions between those states.

Use-case diagrams summarize actor goals, sequence diagrams order interactions across participants, and class diagrams describe static types and relationships. An activity diagram models workflow and action/control flow. Persistent lifecycle states and event-triggered transitions of a particular object instead call for a state machine. The revised third statement makes that mismatch explicit; the original generic event wording was too broad because activities can also respond to events.

Evidence in the complete study note

An activity diagram models workflow: filled circle start, rounded actions, guarded decision diamond, thick fork/join bars and partitions/swimlanes for responsibility. A diamond can also merge alternative flows; a join synchronizes concurrent flows. A state machine models states and transitions triggered by events, often with guards/actions, for one object’s lifecycle.SE20
Sequence diagrams show interactions across lifelines, with order/time generally downward. Messages cross between participants; activation rectangles show execution. A creation message starts a lifeline; an X marks modeled destruction, not a guarantee about when a garbage collector runs. Synchronous calls wait for completion; asynchronous messages permit the sender to proceed.SE19
A class box lists name, attributes and operations; + public, - private, # protected and ~ package indicate visibility. A class diagram shows static types and relationships, while an object diagram shows particular instances/links.SE17

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Use-case diagrams summarize external roles and system goals/interactions.

B · incorrect — Sequence diagrams show ordered participant interactions.

C · correct — The specified lifecycle-state behavior belongs to a state machine rather than an activity workflow.

D · incorrect — Class diagrams describe static classes and their relationships.

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

Correct answer: G — Traceability traces the overall cost and schedule of every activity in the requirement

Traceability records where requirements came from, how requirements depend on one another, and how each requirement is realized and checked in design, code and tests. Source links support rationale, and forward or backward links support change-impact analysis. A cost-and-schedule ledger instead belongs to project planning and control. It can reference requirements, but recording every activity’s cost and schedule is not the definition of requirements traceability.

Evidence in the complete study note

Trace each requirement backward to its source/rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Record dependencies among requirements. A traceability matrix links these artifacts and helps impact analysis; it is not just a cost/schedule ledger. Stakeholders must negotiate conflicting requirements rather than independently approving incompatible demands. Scope, understanding and volatility are distinct elicitation difficulties.SE11

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

Correct answer: A — Pareto principle

Pareto’s 80/20 idea is a prioritization heuristic: a relatively small set of causes may account for a large share of observed impact. It encourages examining evidence to focus improvement effort. It does not promise that exactly one fifth of the effort fixes exactly four fifths of all defects. The revised question asks for this named heuristic, so the other principle names do not identify the rule described.

Evidence in the complete study note

Pareto’s 80/20 rule is a prioritization heuristic: a small subset of causes may account for much of the observed impact. It does not guarantee 80% of defects can be fixed with exactly 20% effort. Refactor to preserve behavior while improving structure; optimize only against measured needs; record rationale and update traceability and regression evidence after change.SE43

Correct answer: C — Agile development method

The scenario’s organizing emphasis is repeated customer collaboration and adaptive planning as needs change, which identifies Agile. Spiral can also accommodate change, but organizes its cycles around explicit risk assessment and reduction. Question 162

Which software process model will you use if you want to deliver different functionalities (modules) of the software product that have different priority at different time?

  • A. Waterfall model
  • B. Spiral model
  • C. Incremental model
  • D. Linear model

Source

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 89

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: C — Incremental model

Incremental development delivers prioritized functionality in usable stages. Earlier increments provide value while later increments add further capability. This is a delivery organization, distinct from a strict single-pass waterfall sequence. Spiral cycles are organized around risks and may use increments, but risk-driven development is not the specific name of the stated delivery strategy. A generic linear sequence also does not describe prioritized usable subsets.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose incremental delivery when prioritized partial capability must reach users early. Smaller changes can be easier to debug and permit feedback, though architecture and integration still require planning. Iteration need not rebuild the whole system every time, and increments need not be perfectly independent modules. Broad descriptions of early working software can fit prototypes, iterative or Agile processes; identify the purpose of that early version.SE04
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall organizes phases before the principal usable delivery.

B · incorrect — Spiral is defined by risk-driven cycles, even when an increment is produced.

C · correct — Incremental development names the successive delivery of usable functionality.

D · incorrect — A linear model does not name prioritized delivery of separate usable subsets.

Question 163

Which of the following is a resource optimization techniques in which start and finish dates are adjusted based on resource constraints with the goal of balancing the demand for resources with the available supply?

  • B. Responsibility assignment matrix
  • C. Resource leveling
  • D. Resource grouping

Study-guide sections

SE31 · Business value, risks and resource optimization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE31 · Business value, risks and resource optimization

Correct answer: C — Resource leveling.

SE31 defines resource leveling as adjusting dates to respect resource availability, potentially changing the project finish. That matches balancing resource demand against supply by moving starts and finishes. Smoothing instead works within available float and schedule constraints. A responsibility matrix assigns ownership, and resource grouping is not the defined date-adjustment technique.

Evidence in the complete study note

Avoidance changes the plan to remove a risk, mitigation reduces likelihood/impact, transfer assigns consequences contractually, and retention/acceptance keeps the risk; passive acceptance may take no action. Resource leveling adjusts dates to respect resource availability and can change project finish; smoothing uses available float within schedule constraints. Neither magically creates extra staff.SE31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Smoothing uses available float while retaining schedule constraints rather than generally leveling against availability.

B · incorrect — A responsibility assignment matrix maps work to owners rather than adjusting task dates for resource capacity.

C · correct — Resource leveling changes dates to balance required resources against available supply.

D · incorrect — Resource grouping is not the defined schedule-adjustment method described by the stem.

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

Correct answer: C — design should be reinventing the wheel from scratch

Reusable classes, controlled change and traceability to requirements support software engineering. Recreating existing solutions from scratch contradicts its reuse rationale.

Evidence in the complete study note

Use abstraction and decomposition to manage complexity; preserve consistency, traceability and clear responsibilities. Top-down design refines high-level structure; bottom-up design assembles existing components. A hybrid combines both. SOLID includes Single Responsibility, Open–Closed, Liskov substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion. Depend on abstractions; add compatible extensions; avoid forcing unused operations. DRY limits duplicated knowledge, KISS avoids unnecessary complexity, and YAGNI avoids speculative work.SE25

Question 167

Study-guide sections

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Correct answer: B — Scrum.

SE05 presents Scrum through timeboxed Sprints, a Sprint Goal and a usable Increment, in the Agile context. Waterfall and the V-model organize planned stages and corresponding tests, while spiral is defined by risk-driven cycles. Therefore Scrum is the specifically Agile approach among the listed alternatives; iteration alone does not make every process Scrum.

Evidence in the complete study note

Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall organizes planned phases rather than the Agile Scrum approach described.

B · correct — Scrum is the Agile framework using Sprints and usable Increments.
