D · incorrect — Spiral is risk driven and is not the specifically Agile methodology named among these choices.

Question 168

A team delivers small usable capabilities, replans the next work with customers and treats adaptation as a central value rather than organizing cycles around risk analysis. Which broad approach best fits?

  • A. Waterfall model
  • B. Agile methodology
  • C. Prototype model
  • D. Spiral model

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 4

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Correct answer: B — Agile methodology

The team adds small usable capabilities and repeatedly replans with customers. Agile makes this combination of working results, customer participation and adaptation central. A prototype’s immediate purpose is learning about requirements or feasibility; a spiral cycle is organized around risk reduction. Classical waterfall instead emphasizes planned phase commitments. Increments by themselves can occur in several processes, so the collaboration and planning priorities establish the intended comparison.

Evidence in the complete study note

Iteration revisits and improves a solution; an increment adds usable functionality. A process may do both. Delivering registration first, then payments, then reporting is incremental; revising a registration prototype after feedback is iterative. Each increment still needs design, implementation and testing.SE04
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06
Agile favors people collaborating, useful working results, customer participation and adaptation over rigid adherence to procedures, exhaustive documents, contracts or fixed plans. The latter still have value. Agile does not mean no planning or no documentation. A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall does not make repeated adaptive replanning its organizing emphasis.

B · correct — Agile combines working increments with ongoing customer collaboration and adaptation.

C · incorrect — Prototyping primarily explores uncertainty rather than naming this ongoing delivery-and-planning organization.

D · incorrect — Spiral’s defining emphasis is risk analysis and reduction.

Question 170

  • B. Class diagrams
  • C. Sequence diagrams

Study-guide sections

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

Correct answers (select all): C, D — Sequence diagrams; State machine diagrams

Sequence diagrams show ordered messages across participant lifelines, while state machines show event-triggered transitions through an object’s lifecycle states. Both therefore describe behavioral evolution over time under the stated scope. A use-case diagram summarizes external roles and goals without that detailed temporal evolution, and a class diagram describes static types and relationships. Neither replaces the two detailed dynamic views requested.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose a sequence diagram for message order between participants, a state machine for event-dependent state changes, and activity for workflow. Both sequence and state diagrams describe behavior over time. State machines are useful for objects with significant states, whether entity or control. A DFD shows data stores/flows and transformations from inputs to outputs; it is not a UML diagram.SE20

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Use-case diagrams summarize roles/goals rather than detailed temporal evolution.

B · incorrect — Class diagrams are static.

A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Question 174

Which testing technique focuses on testing the interaction between different components or modules of a software system?

  • A. Unit testing
  • B. Integration testing
  • C. System testing
  • D. Regression testing

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 10

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: B — Integration testing

Integration testing targets interfaces and interactions among components that have been combined. Unit testing isolates a smaller function or component, while system testing evaluates the complete integrated product against its requirements. Regression testing is triggered by a change and looks for unintended effects; it can be performed at several levels. The scenario is categorized by its interaction scope, so integration is the specific level requested.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35
Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Unit testing isolates a function or small component.

B · correct — Integration testing exercises interactions among combined components.

C · incorrect — System testing evaluates the complete product rather than specifically the component interfaces.

D · incorrect — Regression names the after-change purpose, not a particular component-combination level.

Correct answer: B — Open–Closed, within SOLID.

SE25 lists Open–Closed within SOLID and recommends adding compatible extensions. The stem quotes that principle's central idea: support extension while keeping established code stable. DRY, KISS and YAGNI address other concerns. Open–Closed is a design goal achieved through suitable abstractions, rather than a claim that software can never need modification.

Evidence in the complete study note

Use abstraction and decomposition to manage complexity; preserve consistency, traceability and clear responsibilities. Top-down design refines high-level structure; bottom-up design assembles existing components. A hybrid combines both. SOLID includes Single Responsibility, Open–Closed, Liskov substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion. Depend on abstractions; add compatible extensions; avoid forcing unused operations. DRY limits duplicated knowledge, KISS avoids unnecessary complexity, and YAGNI avoids speculative work.SE25

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — DRY limits duplicated knowledge rather than defining openness for extension.

B · correct — SOLID includes the Open–Closed principle explicitly described by the stem.

C · incorrect — KISS favors simple solutions rather than the specific extension-versus-modification relationship.

D · incorrect — YAGNI avoids speculative functionality rather than defining the Open–Closed design goal.

Question 181

Customer representatives stay in close contact with developers and use feedback to reshape the next timeboxed work. Which methodology makes this collaboration and adaptation a foundational priority?

  • A. Waterfall model
  • B. Agile methodology
  • C. V-model
  • D. Spiral model

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 17

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: B — Agile methodology

Frequent stakeholder communication alone is possible in several lifecycles. The scenario additionally gives customer representatives ongoing access to the team and lets feedback reshape the next timeboxed body of work, matching Agile’s collaboration and adaptation values. Waterfall and the V-model primarily organize planned stages, while spiral organizes commitments around risk reduction. The combination of priorities, rather than communication frequency by itself, identifies the intended methodology.

Evidence in the complete study note

Agile favors people collaborating, useful working results, customer participation and adaptation over rigid adherence to procedures, exhaustive documents, contracts or fixed plans. The latter still have value. Agile does not mean no planning or no documentation. A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05
Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Waterfall is defined by planned phase progression, not the stated adaptive collaboration priority.

B · correct — Agile explicitly prioritizes customer collaboration and responding to change.

C · incorrect — The V-model is defined by linked development and testing stages.

D · incorrect — Spiral’s organizing priority is risk assessment and reduction, though stakeholders can participate.

Question 182

Which technique documents an actor’s goal with preconditions, a main success flow, alternative flows and postconditions?

  • A. Use case modeling
  • B. Storyboarding
  • C. Wireframing
  • D. Pair programming

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 18

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

SE-S05 · Exploration artifacts and collaborative implementation

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

SE-S05 · Exploration artifacts and collaborative implementation

Correct answer: A — Use case modeling

A use-case description captures an actor’s goal together with preconditions, main flow, alternatives and postconditions. This provides the structured behavioral requirements record in the scenario. Storyboards illustrate moments in an interaction and wireframes sketch interface structure; either can help discovery without supplying that full behavioral contract. Pair programming organizes two people’s implementation work. It is therefore use-case modeling that directly names the requested requirements representation.

Evidence in the complete study note

An actor is an external role interacting with the system; it can be a person, device or another system. A person may play several roles, and several people may play one role. A primary actor seeks a goal; a supporting actor provides a service. Ask which user groups perform main functions, administer or maintain the system, and which external systems exchange information.SE14
A storyboard sketches a sequence of moments in a proposed interaction, helping people explore how a concept would be used. A wireframe sketches interface structure and the arrangement of content or controls. Both can inform requirements, but neither automatically supplies a complete use-case description with actors, preconditions, flows and postconditions.SE-S05
Pair programming is a way for two programmers to work together on the same implementation task, commonly sharing a workstation with complementary writing and reviewing roles. It is an implementation collaboration practice rather than a replacement for modeling a user goal.SE-S05

Choice by choice

A · correct — Use-case modeling records actors, goals and structured successful and alternative flows.

B · incorrect — Storyboarding sketches interaction moments rather than necessarily supplying the full goal-and-flow description.

C · incorrect — Wireframing sketches interface structure and layout.

D · incorrect — Pair programming is collaborative implementation work.

Question 183

  • C. Regression testing

Study-guide sections

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: C — Regression testing.

SE36 defines regression testing by the purpose of detecting unintended effects after change. That includes retesting changed and affected areas to find newly introduced faults. Unit, integration and system testing describe levels or scope; regression tests can be run at any of them, so the change-driven purpose uniquely identifies C.

Evidence in the complete study note

Black-box techniques derive cases from specified behavior; white-box techniques derive them from internal structure; grey-box uses partial internal knowledge. Regression testing checks for unintended effects after change; confirmation testing checks the particular defect repair. Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution and is experience based. Manual/automated describe execution support, not a compulsory black-/white-box classification.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Unit testing defines a small-component scope rather than the purpose of checking change-induced defects.

B · incorrect — Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions, which may be regression-tested but do not define regression.

C · correct — Regression testing retests previously working behavior to detect unintended effects of modifications.

D · incorrect — System testing addresses the complete integrated system rather than specifically the after-change purpose.

Question 188

A team separates a reusable reporting component behind a stable interface so other applications can use it and its implementation can change without rewriting clients. Which benefit most directly captures both goals?

  • A. To improve the readability of the code
  • B. To ensure efficient memory management
  • C. To facilitate code reuse and maintenance
  • D. To minimize the number of software defects

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 24

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: C — To facilitate code reuse and maintenance

A module with a stable interface can be reused in another application, and hiding its implementation allows localized changes without rewriting its clients. Those are reuse and maintenance benefits. Readability may improve as well, but it does not fully describe the two goals stated in the scenario. Modularization does not automatically optimize memory use or eliminate defects; good boundaries and verification still matter.

Evidence in the complete study note

Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Readability may improve, but it does not fully describe reuse across applications and localized change.

B · incorrect — Memory efficiency is not guaranteed by separating modules.

C · correct — Reuse and maintenance directly match the two stated goals.

D · incorrect — Reducing defects can be a benefit, but it does not name the stated reuse-and-change objective.

Question 189

Which type of testing aims to uncover defects in the interaction between different components of a software system?

  • A. Unit testing
  • B. Integration testing
  • C. System testing
  • D. Regression testing

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 25

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: B — Integration testing

The defects sought are in communication or interfaces among combined components, so the applicable level is integration testing. Unit tests concentrate on isolated units and system tests assess the complete product. Regression testing instead describes checking for unintended effects after a change, and can include unit, integration or system tests. The distinction is between the scope of combination and the purpose that triggers a test run.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35
Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Unit testing concentrates on an isolated function or small component.

B · correct — Integration testing targets interactions among combined parts.

C · incorrect — System testing checks the whole integrated system against requirements.

D · incorrect — Regression is an after-change objective that can occur at several testing levels.

Question 190

Which programming paradigm is based on the concept of objects and their interactions?

  • A. Functional programming
  • B. Procedural programming
  • C. Object-oriented programming
  • D. Event-driven programming

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 26

Study-guide sections

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Correct answer: C — Object-oriented programming

Object-oriented programming organizes a system around objects that combine state and behavior and interact through operations. Procedural programming decomposes work into functions or procedures that manipulate data. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects, while event-driven programming organizes reactions to events. An object-oriented program may also use events or functions, but the question asks which paradigm is defined by objects and their interactions.

Evidence in the complete study note

Procedural decomposition organizes functions; object oriented decomposition organizes objects with state and behavior. Either can use iterative or sequential development. OOP does not automatically shorten every project. Reuse, encapsulation and consistent models can reduce duplication and ease change; poor object design can still be complex. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects; event-driven programs react to events.SE01

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Functional programming emphasizes evaluation of functions and controlled side effects.

B · incorrect — Procedural programming emphasizes functions or procedures operating on data.

C · correct — Object-oriented programming centers on objects with state and behavior.

D · incorrect — Event-driven programming centers on reactions to events, independent of object-based decomposition.

Version control records artifact versions and their history, making it possible to inspect changes, maintain branches and combine compatible work. SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

Correct answer: A — Waterfall model

Documentation records requirements and architecture so developers can understand decisions, revisit designs and coordinate later change. A user manual is one audience-specific part of this broader purpose.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Correct answer: B — Agile methodology

A fixed short timebox with usable results and customer-driven adaptation of later content fits Agile planning. Classical waterfall and the V-model organize planned development stages, with the latter pairing stages to tests. Spiral cycles organize commitments around risk assessment and reduction. All can incorporate some staged work, so the stated treatment of feedback and later scope is what makes the Agile option the most direct match.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose incremental delivery when prioritized partial capability must reach users early. Smaller changes can be easier to debug and permit feedback, though architecture and integration still require planning. Iteration need not rebuild the whole system every time, and increments need not be perfectly independent modules. Broad descriptions of early working software can fit prototypes, iterative or Agile processes; identify the purpose of that early version.SE04
Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06
Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05

Question 195

Which design principle advocates for designing software components that have a single responsibility?

  • A. Encapsulation
  • B. Inheritance
  • C. Polymorphism
  • D. Single Responsibility Principle

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 31

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE25 · Design principles and operation contracts

SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

Correct answer: D — Single Responsibility Principle.

SE25 identifies Single Responsibility among the core design principles. The question asks directly for one responsibility per component, so D is the exact named rule. Encapsulation protects internal decisions, inheritance creates subtype relations, and polymorphism supports varying implementations through a common interface. Those can help a design but do not themselves define a single responsibility.

Evidence in the complete study note

SOLID includes Single Responsibility, Open–Closed, Liskov substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion.SE25
Generalization places common concepts in a more general superclass and specialized concepts in subclasses. Available inherited attributes and operations are shared by subclasses, which may extend or override behavior.SE-S02
Encapsulation groups state with operations and hides representation behind an interface. Polymorphism permits different object types to respond differently through a common operation or interface. Abstraction exposes the relevant contract while omitting unnecessary detail. Reusability means using suitable existing classes or components in new contexts rather than writing them again. These ideas support each other but name different properties.SE-S02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Encapsulation hides implementation details rather than requiring one responsibility per component.

B · incorrect — Inheritance establishes superclass/subclass reuse rather than the focused-responsibility rule.

C · incorrect — Polymorphism supports compatible varying implementations rather than defining responsibility count.

D · correct — Single Responsibility explicitly calls for one focused responsibility in a software component.

Question 196

Which design pattern is used to ensure that only one instance of a class is created throughout the system?

  • A. Singleton pattern
  • B. Factory pattern
  • C. Observer pattern
  • D. Decorator pattern

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 32

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE27 · Patterns, variability and testability

Correct answer: A — Singleton.

SE27 describes Singleton as controlling access to one instance. That is the pattern requested by the one-instance condition. Factory patterns address how concrete objects are created, Observer notifies subscribers and Decorator adds behavior by wrapping. None of those other pattern responsibilities guarantees a single shared instance by itself.

Evidence in the complete study note

Factory Method lets subclasses choose a concrete product through a creation operation, reducing coupling to concrete constructors. A simple factory centralizes creation but is not identical to Factory Method. Singleton controls access to one instance; Observer notifies subscribers; Memento stores/restores state while hiding representation; Iterator traverses; Decorator adds behavior through wrapping. The pattern name is Memento, not Momento.SE27

Choice by choice

A · correct — Singleton controls creation and access so that the intended class has one shared instance.

B · incorrect — A factory selects or constructs products rather than inherently limiting a class to one instance.

C · incorrect — Observer distributes notifications to subscribers rather than restricting object instance count.

D · incorrect — Decorator adds behavior through wrapping rather than enforcing a single instance.

Question 197

Which test type checks that specified services produce the required outputs under normal operating conditions, without measuring speed/resources or user task ease?

  • A. Stress testing
  • B. Performance testing
  • C. Functional testing
  • D. Usability testing

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 33

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: C — Functional testing

Functional tests compare observable services and outputs with the SRS and acceptance criteria. That is the stated objective, so C applies. Performance testing measures speed, throughput or resources, and usability evaluates user task success or ease; neither is requested here. Stress testing exceeds normal limits. Normal operating conditions alone would not distinguish these types, but the explicit behavioral objective does.

Evidence in the complete study note

Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Stress testing exceeds normal operating limits.

B · incorrect — Performance testing measures speed, throughput or resources.

C · correct — Functional testing checks specified services and outputs.

D · incorrect — Usability testing evaluates user task ease or success.

Question 198

Which programming paradigm promotes the use of data and avoids side effects?

  • A. Functional programming
  • B. Procedural programming
  • C. Object-oriented programming
  • D. Event-driven programming

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 34

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

Correct answer: A — Functional programming, for the side-effect emphasis.

The phrase promotes the use of data is not distinctive because all these paradigms use data. The discriminating part is avoiding or controlling side effects. SE01 explicitly assigns function evaluation and controlled side effects to functional programming. Procedural, object-oriented and event-driven styles organize behavior differently and do not inherently impose that emphasis.

Evidence in the complete study note

Procedural decomposition organizes functions; object oriented decomposition organizes objects with state and behavior. Either can use iterative or sequential development. OOP does not automatically shorten every project. Reuse, encapsulation and consistent models can reduce duplication and ease change; poor object design can still be complex. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects; event-driven programs react to events.SE01

Choice by choice

A · correct — Functional programming emphasizes evaluating functions and controlling side effects.

B · incorrect — Procedural decomposition organizes functions or procedures without inherently avoiding state-changing effects.

C · incorrect — Object-oriented decomposition combines state and behavior and does not inherently exclude side effects.

D · incorrect — Event-driven programs react to events; that does not itself require avoiding side effects.

Question 199

Which type of software maintenance involves making changes to a software system to adapt it to new environments or technologies?

  • A. Corrective maintenance
  • B. Adaptive maintenance
  • C. Perfective maintenance
  • D. Preventive maintenance

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 35

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk.

Study-guide sections

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

Correct answer: B — Adaptive maintenance.

SE40 defines adaptive maintenance as responding to changes in the environment. New platforms or technologies therefore create an adaptive-maintenance need even when the original software is not faulty. Corrective maintenance fixes faults, perfective work improves useful capability or performance, and preventive work reduces future risk. The stated environmental motive makes B the appropriate category.

Evidence in the complete study note

Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Corrective work fixes faults rather than primarily accommodating changed environments or technology.

B · correct — Adaptive maintenance changes software so it continues working in a new environment or technology context.

C · incorrect — Perfective work improves capability or performance rather than specifically responding to an environmental change.

D · incorrect — Preventive work reduces future maintenance risk rather than defining adaptation to a new environment.

Question 201

Which software development methodology involves iterative development cycles called sprints?

  • A. Waterfall model
  • B. Agile methodology
  • C. Spiral model
  • D. V-model

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 37

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

Correct answer: B — Agile methodology, specifically Scrum.

SE05 places Sprints in Scrum, an Agile framework. B is therefore the available category that contains the specific process described. Agile as a whole does not require every method to call its iterations Sprints. Waterfall, spiral and the V-model have other organizing principles, so none is the named Sprint-based method.

Evidence in the complete study note

Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall uses planned phases rather than Scrum Sprints.

B · correct — Scrum is an Agile framework whose iterative delivery cycles are called Sprints.

C · incorrect — Spiral uses risk-driven cycles rather than specifically the Scrum Sprint mechanism.

D · incorrect — The V-model pairs development stages with tests rather than organizing work into Sprints.

Question 202

What is the primary purpose of code refactoring?

  • A. To add new features to the software system
  • B. To optimize the performance of the software system
  • C. To improve the readability and maintainability of the code
  • D. To fix defects or issues in the software system

Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

Study-guide sections

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE43 · Design choices, evidence and economical improvement

Correct answer: C — To improve the readability and maintainability of the code

Restructuring explicitly addresses maintainability, readability and understandability, while optimization separately addresses speed and memory. C matches refactoring’s purpose of improving internal structure and maintainability.

Evidence in the complete study note

Pareto’s 80/20 rule is a prioritization heuristic: a small subset of causes may account for much of the observed impact. It does not guarantee 80% of defects can be fixed with exactly 20% effort. Refactor to preserve behavior while improving structure; optimize only against measured needs; record rationale and update traceability and regression evidence after change.SE43

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Adds behavior, whereas restructuring reorganizes existing design elements. See PDF p. 133.

B · incorrect — Optimization is separately classified by performance goals. See PDF p. 133.

C · correct — Direct match to the documented restructuring goals. See PDF p. 133.

D · incorrect — Repairing a fault is correction; restructuring need not fix a behavioral defect. See PDF p. 133.

Question 203

Which approach treats customer participation in reviewing working results and reprioritizing future work as a foundational value, rather than merely a practice a project may choose?

  • A. Waterfall model
  • B. Agile methodology
  • C. Spiral model
  • D. V-model

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 39

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: B — Agile methodology

The project treats customer participation in reviewing results and reprioritizing future work as a foundational development value. This directly matches Agile’s customer collaboration and responsiveness to change. Waterfall and the V-model primarily define phase and test-stage organization. Spiral also includes stakeholder review, but risk assessment and reduction define its cycle. Participation alone is not exclusive; the explicit priority given to continual adaptive collaboration identifies the answer.

Evidence in the complete study note

Agile favors people collaborating, useful working results, customer participation and adaptation over rigid adherence to procedures, exhaustive documents, contracts or fixed plans. The latter still have value. Agile does not mean no planning or no documentation. A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05
Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Classical waterfall’s defining organization is planned phase progression.

B · correct — Agile explicitly prioritizes customer collaboration and adapting to feedback.

C · incorrect — Spiral includes review but is defined by risk-driven cycles.

D · incorrect — The V-model organizes linked development and test stages, rather than naming the stated collaboration values.

Question 204

Which type of testing involves running the entire software system in an environment that closely resembles the production environment?

  • A. Unit testing
  • B. Integration testing
  • C. System testing
  • D. Regression testing

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 40

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

Correct answer: C — System testing

System testing evaluates the complete integrated software against its functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment. Unit testing isolates a smaller element and integration testing concentrates on interfaces among combined parts. Regression testing instead checks for unintended consequences after change and is not restricted to any one level or environment. The question specifies the complete-product scope, making system testing the direct classification.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35
Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component.

B · incorrect — Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions among combined parts.

C · correct — System testing evaluates the complete integrated product in a representative environment.

D · incorrect — Regression names an after-change checking purpose and can run at multiple levels.

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

Correct answer: C — A sequence of activities performed by a user or system

A use case describes a system-provided function as a flow of events producing an actor-visible result. C is acceptable when understood as goal-related interactions, not any arbitrary sequence of activities.

Draw actors outside the system boundary rectangle and use-case ovals inside. Name a goal with a verb and noun. The diagram shows roles, goals and relationships, not the full detailed algorithm or UI layout. Question 206

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

Correct answer: B — An external interacting role played by a person, device or another system.

An actor is an external role that interacts across the chosen system boundary. A person, device or another system may play that role. It is not an internal component, a diagram, or merely one individual user account. Because actors model roles rather than particular people, one person can play multiple actors and multiple people can fulfill the same actor role.

Evidence in the complete study note

Draw actors outside the system boundary rectangle and use-case ovals inside. Name a goal with a verb and noun. The diagram shows roles, goals and relationships, not the full detailed algorithm or UI layout. Being an internal component is different from being an external actor; the chosen boundary determines which role applies.SE14
An actor is an external role interacting with the system; it can be a person, device or another system. A person may play several roles, and several people may play one role.SE14

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — An internal component is not an external actor merely because it acts.

Study-guide sections

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Correct answer: A — To represent the reuse of common steps between use cases

Factoring common functionality into one included use case eliminates redundant descriptions, as in shared HelpDispatcher behavior.

Evidence in the complete study note

Include factors required reused behavior: Submit Order includes Validate Order, with the dashed arrow from the including/base use case to the included one. Extend adds conditional behavior at extension points: Apply Discount extends Checkout, with the arrow from the extension to the base. The base is meaningful independently. For an extension, draw the arrow from the extending use case to the base use case.SE16

Choice by choice

A · correct — Direct reuse/commonality mechanism. See PDF p. 50, 50.

B · incorrect — Optional exceptional behavior is more directly represented by extend. See PDF p. 50, 50.

C · incorrect — Adds events under conditions through extend rather than reuse via include. See PDF p. 50, 50.

D · incorrect — Actor/use-case communication uses associations, not include. See PDF p. 50, 50.

Question 208

Which statements describe extend between use cases? Select all that apply. Read optional as conditional behavior at an extension point.

  • A. To factor required reused steps into an included use case.
  • B. To represent optional steps within a use case

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Correct answers (select all): B, C — To represent optional steps within a use case; To represent the extension of a use case with additional steps

Extend adds conditional behavior at extension points in an independently meaningful base use case. It therefore represents optional additional behavior and extends the base with added steps, making both B and C true. Factoring required reused behavior is the include relationship. Associations between actors and use cases are separate from the extend relationship linking use cases to one another.

Evidence in the complete study note

Include factors required reused behavior: Submit Order includes Validate Order, with the dashed arrow from the including/base use case to the included one. Extend adds conditional behavior at extension points: Apply Discount extends Checkout, with the arrow from the extension to the base. The base is meaningful independently. For an extension, draw the arrow from the extending use case to the base use case.SE16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Required reused behavior is factored with include.

B · correct — Conditional additional behavior need not occur in every base execution.

C · correct — Extend adds steps to an independently meaningful base.

D · incorrect — Actor association is a different relationship.

Question 210

What defines an abstract use case, rather than optionality, unfinished documentation or reuse alone?

  • A. To represent a use case that is not yet fully defined
  • B. To represent a use case that is optional in the system
  • C. It specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case.
  • D. To represent a use case that is reused by other use cases

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 46

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

Correct answer: C — It specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case.

An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. That is different from being unfinished, optional or reused. Concrete behavior can be included for reuse, and extend can express conditional additions. Nor does the absence of a direct actor line by itself establish abstraction. Option C states the actual defining criterion.

Evidence in the complete study note

Generalization relates a specialized actor/use case to a more general one, with a hollow triangle toward the general element. An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. It is not defined merely by reuse or lack of a direct actor line. Included behavior is incorporated where the inclusion is reached; do not infer every conditional branch in the base always executes.SE16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — An incomplete description is not the abstraction criterion.

B · incorrect — Optional behavior is not the abstraction criterion.

C · correct — Specialization without direct complete instantiation defines this abstraction.

D · incorrect — Reuse alone can also involve concrete use cases.

Question 211

Which option states the most specific defining purpose of an exception flow, distinguishing it from a generic alternative flow?

  • A. To represent an error or exceptional situation in the use case
  • B. To represent an alternative path within the use case
  • C. To represent the termination of the use case
  • D. To represent the relationship between primary and secondary actors

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 47

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE15 · Write a complete use case with alternatives

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE15 · Write a complete use case with alternatives

Correct answer: A — To represent an error or exceptional situation in the use case

An exception flow handles an error or failure encountered in the use case. Such a path is also an alternative to the main success flow in a broad sense, but B alone does not distinguish exceptional handling from normal conditional variations. An exception may allow correction and recovery instead of terminating the use case. Actor relationships do not define its failure-handling purpose.

Evidence in the complete study note

Example: Submit Incident. Precondition: officer authenticated. 1 Officer supplies location and description. 2 System validates details. 3 System records the incident. 4 System returns its ID. Alternative 2a: location missing → report the problem and request correction; save nothing. Success postcondition: incident and ID persist; failure guarantee: no partial record. An alternate flow is a conditional variation; an exception flow handles a failure. Preconditions hold before entry, while a trigger starts the use case.SE15

Choice by choice

A · correct — Error or exceptional handling is the specific defining purpose.

B · incorrect — Alternative path is broader and does not identify the exceptional nature.

C · incorrect — Exceptions need not terminate the entire use case.

D · incorrect — Actor relationships do not describe failure handling.

System and software design establish the overall architecture and identify software abstractions and relationships.

System design turns the analysis model into architecture: design goals, subsystem responsibilities, dependencies, hardware mapping, data management, access control, control flow and startup/shutdown/error policies. Question 216

Instead of delivering the system as a single delivery, development and delivery is broken down into phases with each phase delivering part of the required functionality. What type of development model is this?

  • A. Incremental
  • B. Waterfall
  • C. Spiral
  • D. Evolutionary

Source

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 8

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Study-guide sections

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

SE06 · Spiral development and risk

Correct answer: A — Incremental

Successive deliveries that each add part of the required usable functionality define incremental development. The product gains capability across these deliveries rather than waiting for a single completed-system handoff. Waterfall and a generic linear model organize phase sequence. Spiral is organized around risk assessment, and evolutionary development broadly describes refinement. Those can overlap with staged delivery, but incremental is the specific name for the delivery organization stated.

Evidence in the complete study note

Choose incremental delivery when prioritized partial capability must reach users early. Smaller changes can be easier to debug and permit feedback, though architecture and integration still require planning. Iteration need not rebuild the whole system every time, and increments need not be perfectly independent modules. Broad descriptions of early working software can fit prototypes, iterative or Agile processes; identify the purpose of that early version.SE04
Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

Choice by choice

A · correct — Incremental development adds usable required functionality in successive deliveries.

B · incorrect — Waterfall names planned phase progression, not this particular staged-capability strategy.

C · incorrect — Spiral names risk-driven cycles, even when increments are produced.

D · incorrect — Evolutionary refinement is broader than the specific addition-of-functionality strategy described.

Question 217

Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

Correct answer: D — Software requirements change quickly

Waterfall should be used only when requirements are well understood and unlikely to change radically. Rapid requirement change violates this selection condition.

Evidence in the complete study note

Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03

A · incorrect — Available expertise is not the documented contraindication. See PDF p. 20.

B · incorrect — Unambiguous stable requirements support, rather than undermine, the model. See PDF p. 20.

C · incorrect — The module says waterfall works well for smaller projects with well-understood requirements. See PDF p. 20.

D · correct — Directly violates the stability assumption and creates costly rework. See PDF p. 20.

Which one of the following is false about divide and conquer or modularization process?

  • A. Separate people can work on each sub-divided part

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

Correct answer: D — Replacing or changing a component is difficult because it affects other parts extremely

Subsystems can be assigned to separate teams, reused and changed with reduced impact when coupled loosely. D contradicts the change-isolation goal of good modularization.

Evidence in the complete study note

Logical cohesion groups similar-category operations, often selected by a flag; temporal cohesion groups operations done at the same time; functional cohesion focuses on one task. Splitting an unrelated three-purpose component improves modularity. If behavior is preserved, the restructuring is refactoring; the words are not mutually exclusive answers. Smaller modules can aid understanding, independent work, reuse and maintenance, but too many interfaces also create complexity.SE22

Question 219

For this project, planned testing effort in hours is setup + (cases × hours per case). The estimates (setup,cases,hours/case) are Unit=(4,80,0.1), Acceptance=(3,10,1), System=(6,20,0.5), Integration=(4,20,0.5). Which level has the greatest planned effort?

  • A. Unit testing
  • B. Acceptance testing
  • C. System testing
  • D. Integration testing

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 13

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the effort formula given in the question separately for every level, then compare all computed totals.

Study-guide sections

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE28 · Planning, WBS, estimation and tools

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

SE28 · Planning, WBS, estimation and tools

Correct answer: C — System testing

The estimates give unit effort 4+80×0.1=12 hours, acceptance 3+10×1=13, system 6+20×0.5=16, and integration 4+20×0.5=14. System testing therefore has the greatest planned effort for this project. The note does not make any test level universally longest; the explicit workload and setup assumptions are what justify this particular ranking.

Evidence in the complete study note

Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35
None of these levels is universally the longest.SE35
Planning is continuous: identify scope/deliverables, decompose work, estimate effort/duration/cost, assign resources, sequence dependencies and revise as evidence changes.SE28

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Unit totals twelve hours, below the maximum.

B · incorrect — Acceptance totals thirteen hours, below the maximum.

C · correct — System totals sixteen hours, the largest estimate.

D · incorrect — Integration totals fourteen hours, below system testing.

Question 220

A filled composition diamond is at Car’s end of its Engine association. In this model Engine remains owned for its entire lifetime and cannot be detached or transferred. What does this imply?

  • A. Car uses Engine temporarily
  • B. Engine can exist independently of the Car
  • C. Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy.
  • D. Car inherits from Engine

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 10

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

Study-guide sections

SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

Correct answer: C — Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy.

Composition makes Engine a strongly owned part of Car, with the filled diamond beside the whole. Parts still owned are destroyed when their composite is destroyed. Since this model does not permit Engine to detach or transfer, it cannot continue an independent lifetime without Car. Temporary use would be a dependency, and inheritance would be shown by a hollow triangle.

Evidence in the complete study note

Composition uses a filled diamond at the whole end and strong ownership: a part is in at most one composite at a time, and parts still owned are destroyed with that composite. Parts may be detached/transferred under a defined model. Thus “cannot ever exist independently” is an oversimplification. For Car composing Engine, the diamond belongs beside Car; saying it points to Engine is imprecise. The Car–Engine example describes composition.SE18

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Temporary use is a dependency rather than composition.

B · incorrect — The no-detachment policy excludes an independent Engine lifetime.

C · correct — Engine is Car’s owned part and cannot outlive it under this policy.

D · incorrect — Inheritance uses a hollow triangle.

Study-guide references

SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

SE03 says waterfall fits stable understood requirements and familiar technology. Late feedback can make changes costly, so moderate-to-high requirement-change risk is a direct disadvantage. Simplicity and milestone visibility are advantages. Sequential phase organization characterizes the classical model; it can contribute to rigidity, but C explicitly identifies the adverse scenario asked for.

Evidence in the complete study note

Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03

Question 222

For a search service whose functions and database technology are already specified, which requirement adds a quantitative service-speed target?

  • A. The system allow user to generate PDF report.
  • B. The system respond to user’s request within 2 second under normal load
  • C. The system allow user to store data on relational database
  • D. The system allow user to submit emergency report

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 61

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

Study-guide sections

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

Correct answer: B — The system respond to user’s request within 2 second under normal load

The two-second response obligation bounds the speed of a service under the stated load, so it is a performance requirement. Generating a PDF and submitting an emergency report describe services the system provides. The database clause describes storage behavior together with an implementation choice; it does not impose a response-time threshold. The explicit performance scope removes the broader taxonomy overlap between nonfunctional requirements and technology constraints.

Evidence in the complete study note

Nonfunctional requirements include quality attributes and constraints. Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning. Security concerns protection; compatibility concerns cooperating environments; portability concerns moving environments; maintainability/supportability concern change, diagnosis and evolution.SE10
“Search responds within two seconds under 100 concurrent users” is measurable performance. “New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability. “Use Java” is a technology/pseudo-requirement, often separately classified as a system constraint. Dependability includes reliability, safety and robustness; portability is not its usual central category. Performance degradation at peak load primarily concerns performance, not automatically reliability.SE10

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Report generation specifies a service, not its response-time limit.

B · correct — A two-second response bound under normal load is a quantitative speed target.

C · incorrect — This specifies storage behavior and a database technology, without a timing bound.

D · incorrect — Submitting an emergency report specifies a function rather than its speed.

Question 223

Which one of the following UML building block that defines the static part of the model and represents physical and conceptual elements?

  • B. Behavioral things
  • C. An notational things
  • D. Grouping things

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 80

SE17 · Class diagrams, visibility and multiplicity

SE-S03 · Modeling categories and data diagrams

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

SE17 · Class diagrams, visibility and multiplicity

SE-S03 · Modeling categories and data diagrams

Correct answer: A — Structural things.

SE17 explicitly describes structural things as conceptual or physical structural elements. They make up the static model in contrast with behavior over time. Behavioral things cover dynamic aspects, grouping organizes elements and annotations add explanatory information rather than being the static elements themselves. Thus A directly matches both parts of the definition.

Evidence in the complete study note

A class box lists name, attributes and operations; + public, - private, # protected and ~ package indicate visibility. A class diagram shows static types and relationships, while an object diagram shows particular instances/links. UML is maintained and standardized by OMG; it is a modeling language, not a lifecycle process. Structural things describe conceptual or physical structural elements.SE17
In the course’s UML building-block terminology, structural things describe static conceptual or physical elements. Behavioral things describe dynamic interactions and state behavior. Grouping things organize model elements into packages. Annotational things attach explanatory remarks or constraints, usually as notes.SE-S03

Choice by choice

A · correct — Structural things are the static conceptual or physical building blocks described.

B · incorrect — Behavioral things concern dynamic behavior rather than the static structural elements.

C · incorrect — Annotations add explanatory information rather than defining the static structural building blocks.
