Question 224

What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements? Give an example of each.

    Source

    • Software Engineering review questions · Question 1

    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

    Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

    Study-guide sections

    SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

    SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

    Answer & Detailed Explanation

    Study-guide references

    SE09 · Functional requirements include prohibited behavior

    SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

    Answer: Functional requirements specify observable behavior; nonfunctional requirements specify qualities or constraints. Example: generate a PDF report versus respond within two seconds under a stated load.

    SE09 includes required and prohibited services, so generating a PDF report is functional. SE10 specifies qualities such as performance, usability and availability; a response-time threshold under defined load is nonfunctional. Security mechanisms can implement functional behavior as well as support quality goals, so a negative or security-related statement is not automatically nonfunctional.

    Evidence in the complete study note

    A functional requirement states an observable service or behavior, including reactions to inputs, errors and forbidden actions. “When the sensor detects intrusion, send an alert” is functional.SE09
    “The system shall generate a PDF report” is functional. “The system shall not reveal another customer’s balance” can be a security-related functional rule. Security as a broad quality goal and the functions implementing it must be distinguished.SE09
    Nonfunctional requirements include quality attributes and constraints. Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning.SE10
    “Search responds within two seconds under 100 concurrent users” is measurable performance. “New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability.SE10

    Question 225

    Why is low coupling considered good in software design?

      Source

      • Software Engineering review questions · Question 2

      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

      Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

      Study-guide sections

      SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

      Answer & Detailed Explanation

      Study-guide references

      SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

      Answer: Low coupling limits dependencies, so changes remain local and modules are easier to understand, replace, test and maintain.

      SE22 measures coupling through dependencies between modules and recommends low coupling with high cohesion. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s representation increase the chance that one change affects others. Stable interfaces and information hiding constrain that impact. More interfaces can add complexity, so minimizing harmful dependencies matters more than simply maximizing the number of modules.

      Evidence in the complete study note

      Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22

      Question 226

      What is the difference between Waterfall and Agile methodologies?

        Source

        • Software Engineering review questions · Question 3

        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

        Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

        Study-guide sections

        SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

        SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

        Answer & Detailed Explanation

        Study-guide references

        SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

        SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

        Answer: Waterfall uses planned, reviewed stages and suits stable requirements; Agile emphasizes collaboration, working results, feedback and adaptation.

        SE03 describes planned phases with costly late feedback, useful for stable requirements and familiar technology. SE05 values customer participation and adaptation with useful working increments. Agile still plans and documents; waterfall can revisit work under control. The practical difference is feedback and commitment organization, not a claim that one process forbids change or the other forbids documentation.

        Evidence in the complete study note

        Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03
        Agile favors people collaborating, useful working results, customer participation and adaptation over rigid adherence to procedures, exhaustive documents, contracts or fixed plans. The latter still have value. Agile does not mean no planning or no documentation. A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05

        Question 227

        What is the difference between <<include>> and <<extend>> in use case diagrams?

          Source

          • Software Engineering review questions · Question 4

          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

          Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

          Study-guide sections

          SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

          Answer & Detailed Explanation

          Study-guide references

          SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

          Answer: Include factors required reused behavior, with base→included; extend adds conditional behavior, with extension→base.

          SE16 uses include for reused required behavior incorporated when the inclusion point is reached. Extend adds behavior at extension points under a condition, and the base remains meaningful independently. The dashed arrows have different directions: including use case toward included, and extending use case toward base. Neither relation should be confused with actor association or specialization generalization.

          Evidence in the complete study note

          Include factors required reused behavior: Submit Order includes Validate Order, with the dashed arrow from the including/base use case to the included one. Extend adds conditional behavior at extension points: Apply Discount extends Checkout, with the arrow from the extension to the base. The base is meaningful independently. For an extension, draw the arrow from the extending use case to the base use case.SE16
          Generalization relates a specialized actor/use case to a more general one, with a hollow triangle toward the general element. An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. It is not defined merely by reuse or lack of a direct actor line. Included behavior is incorporated where the inclusion is reached; do not infer every conditional branch in the base always executes.SE16

          Question 228

          Why is maintenance often the most expensive phase of the SDLC?

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 5

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk.

            Study-guide sections

            SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

            Answer: Maintenance can dominate cost because it lasts years and repeatedly requires legacy understanding, changes, regression testing and release work.

            SE40 says maintenance often spans years and includes understanding existing code plus regression effort. Work is not limited to bug fixes: environments, useful capabilities and future risks also change. Repeated impact analysis, implementation and testing accumulate across the operational lifetime, so maintenance may dominate lifecycle cost. This is a common outcome, not a guarantee for every project.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40
            A typical evolution sequence is change request→impact analysis→release planning→implementation/testing→release. Among a list lacking the request step, impact analysis may be the earliest listed technical activity. Major restructuring is reengineering; if the architecture itself changes, architectural transformation is the more specific description. Markets, technology, stakeholders and funding can all change scope or priorities.SE40

            Question 229

            Which software development approach emphasizes breaking systems into functions or procedures that manipulate isolated data?

            • A. Object-Oriented Approach
            • B. Traditional Approach
            • C. Agile Approach
            • D. Iterative Approach

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 1

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE01 · Software engineering, processes and work products

            Correct answer: B — Traditional/procedural decomposition.

            SE01 contrasts procedural decomposition organized around functions with object-oriented decomposition organized around objects combining state and behavior. B is the available traditional/procedural label for functions operating on data. Agile and iterative describe lifecycle organization rather than this decomposition paradigm, and either can be used with procedural or object-oriented programming.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Procedural decomposition organizes functions; object oriented decomposition organizes objects with state and behavior. Either can use iterative or sequential development. OOP does not automatically shorten every project. Reuse, encapsulation and consistent models can reduce duplication and ease change; poor object design can still be complex. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects; event-driven programs react to events.SE01

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Object orientation combines state and behavior in objects rather than organizing primarily around separate procedures.

            B · correct — Traditional/procedural decomposition organizes functions and procedures acting on data.

            C · incorrect — Agile concerns process adaptation rather than requiring function-based decomposition.

            D · incorrect — Iteration describes revisiting development work and does not determine procedural versus object decomposition.

            Question 230

            In the Object-Oriented Approach, which property allows classes to be used in different parts of the system or other projects without rewriting them?

            • A. Encapsulation
            • B. Polymorphism
            • C. Reusability
            • D. Abstraction

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 2

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

            Study-guide sections

            SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE-S02 · Objects, shared models and specialization

            Correct answer: C — Reusability.

            The stem explicitly asks about using existing classes elsewhere without rewriting them, which is reuse. SE01 lists reuse alongside encapsulation and consistent models as ways to reduce duplication and ease change. Encapsulation and abstraction can make reuse safer, while polymorphism supports compatible varying implementations, but those are enabling concepts rather than the name of the capability described.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Encapsulation groups state with operations and hides representation behind an interface. Polymorphism permits different object types to respond differently through a common operation or interface. Abstraction exposes the relevant contract while omitting unnecessary detail. Reusability means using suitable existing classes or components in new contexts rather than writing them again. These ideas support each other but name different properties.SE-S02

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Encapsulation hides implementation and can enable reuse, but it is not the capability's name.

            B · incorrect — Polymorphism supports differing implementations through compatible interfaces rather than directly naming reuse.

            C · correct — Reusability means using suitable existing classes or components in other contexts without rewriting them.

            D · incorrect — Abstraction exposes relevant contracts and can assist reuse, but the requested property is reusability.

            SE40 · Maintenance and software evolution

            Correct answer: D — Software evolution.

            SE40 describes maintenance and evolution through change requests, impact analysis, planning, implementation/testing and release. Updating a deployed product to meet changing customer needs belongs to evolution among the four broad process activities. Specification, implementation and validation still occur within that work, but D names the lifecycle-wide change activity asked for rather than one constituent task.

            Corrective maintenance fixes faults; adaptive maintenance responds to environment changes; perfective maintenance improves useful capability/performance; preventive maintenance reduces future risk, such as restructuring fragile code. Motive determines category; refactoring can support preventive or perfective work. Maintenance often lasts years and includes understanding legacy code and regression effort, so it may dominate lifecycle cost.SE40
            A typical evolution sequence is change request→impact analysis→release planning→implementation/testing→release.SE40

            Question 232

            A software process that plans all activities in advance and measures progress against that plan is classified as:

            • A. Agile Process
            • B. Plan-Driven Process
            • C. Incremental Process
            • D. Evolutionary Process

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 4

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE-S04 · Plan-driven and adaptive planning

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE-S04 · Plan-driven and adaptive planning

            Correct answer: B — Plan-driven process.

            The stem defines up-front planning and measurement against that plan. B names the plan-driven organization, illustrated by SE03’s planned phases and reviewed deliverables. Incremental delivery and evolution describe how results grow or change and can coexist with planning. Agile also plans, but it emphasizes adaptation rather than defining all activity commitments in advance as stated here.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            In a plan-driven process, activities are planned in advance and progress is assessed against that plan. Agile planning is incremental and adapts to changing needs. This distinction concerns planning strategy; a process can combine advance planning with staged deliveries and feedback.SE-S04

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Agile uses planning but adapts content as feedback arrives rather than defining this fixed up-front emphasis.

            B · correct — Plan-driven explicitly organizes activities and progress measurement around an advance plan.

            C · incorrect — Incremental describes staged capability delivery and does not alone specify up-front planning commitments.

            D · incorrect — Evolutionary describes progressive change rather than necessarily advance planning of all activities.

            Question 233

            In requirement elicitation, the document created to describe what the system should do — agreed upon by clients and developers — is called:

            • B. Use Case Diagram
            • C. Requirements Specification
            • D. Design Document

            Study-guide sections

            SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE08 · Feasibility and levels of requirements

            Correct answer: C — Requirements Specification.

            SE08 states that the Software Requirements Specification organizes agreed requirements. That is the artifact describing what the system should do for client/developer agreement. Analysis models support technical discussion, a use-case diagram captures only selected goals/relationships and a design document describes solution decisions. None replaces the overall agreed requirements specification.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Business requirements explain why the project exists and its goals. User requirements describe stakeholder needs at a useful high level; system requirements specify detailed services and constraints. The Software Requirements Specification (SRS) organizes the agreed requirements. A natural-language specification communicates with clients while analysis models formalize it for technical discussion; real specifications can also contain diagrams.SE08

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Analysis models formalize selected aspects for discussion rather than replacing the full agreed requirements document.

            B · incorrect — A use-case diagram shows goals and roles but not the complete requirements specification.

            C · correct — The requirements specification organizes the agreed services and constraints the system must satisfy.

            D · incorrect — A design document describes how the solution is organized rather than the complete statement of required behavior.

            SE14 · Actors, use cases and scope

            Correct answer: B — External interacting roles played by people, devices or other systems.

            SE14 explicitly permits a person, device or other system to play an external actor role. B is the only option including those categories. Actors are not restricted to primary users or humans, and internal components are inside the chosen system boundary rather than external roles.             Question 236

            Which type of requirement specifies that 'the system must respond within 1 second'?

            • A. Functional Requirement
            • B. System Constraint
            • C. Non-Functional Requirement
            • D. Domain Requirement

            SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

            Correct answer: C — Nonfunctional performance requirement.

            SE10 identifies response time as a performance quality. A one-second threshold constrains how well a service responds rather than naming the service itself, so C is the appropriate category. A complete measurable requirement should also define the operation, load and timing conditions. Those omissions affect test precision, not the underlying classification of the stated response-time target.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Nonfunctional requirements include quality attributes and constraints. Performance concerns response time, throughput and resource use; reliability concerns failure-free service; availability concerns being ready for use; usability concerns task success and ease of learning. Security concerns protection; compatibility concerns cooperating environments; portability concerns moving environments; maintainability/supportability concern change, diagnosis and evolution.SE10

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — The statement constrains response speed rather than specifying which service is performed.

            B · incorrect — The specific quality is performance; this is not primarily a technology or implementation constraint.

            C · correct — The one-second limit is a nonfunctional response-time/performance target.

            D · incorrect — No domain-specific business rule is stated; the obligation concerns a general performance quality.

            Question 237

            SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

            Study-guide references

            SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

            Correct answer: C — System/Constraint Requirement

            The statement prescribes an implementation technology rather than an externally observable service or a measurable product quality. In the course’s explicit separation of quality attributes from technology constraints, the specific category is a system or constraint requirement. A broad requirements taxonomy can place constraints under nonfunctional requirements, but the question asks for the more specific category. No performance, reliability or usability threshold is supplied by merely naming Java.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            “Search responds within two seconds under 100 concurrent users” is measurable performance. “New users finish checkout within one minute without help” is usability. “Use Java” is a technology/pseudo-requirement, often separately classified as a system constraint. Dependability includes reliability, safety and robustness; portability is not its usual central category. Performance degradation at peak load primarily concerns performance, not automatically reliability.SE10

            B · incorrect — This is a broader umbrella in some taxonomies; it is incomplete when the specific constraint category is offered.

            SE10 · Nonfunctional qualities and measurable constraints

            SE-S07 · Scalability and robustness are different qualities

Supporting different browsers and devices in the question is the offered compatibility category.             Question 240

            In requirements elicitation activities, which step involves formalizing scenarios into structured descriptions of system interactions?

            • A. Identifying Actors
            • B. Identifying Use Cases
            • C. Identifying Scenarios
            • D. Refining Use Cases

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 12

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

            Study-guide sections

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Correct answer: B — Identifying use cases by abstracting concrete scenarios.

            SE13 calls a scenario one concrete execution and a use case an abstraction of related success and alternative scenarios. Formalizing those interactions into the more general use-case description therefore identifies use cases. Identifying actors establishes external roles, identifying scenarios captures individual executions and later refinement adds detail to an already identified use case.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A scenario is one concrete execution; a use case abstracts the related successful and alternative scenarios. Analysis integrates functional (use cases/scenarios), structural/object (classes) and dynamic (states/interactions) models. Entity objects represent domain information such as Incident; boundary objects mediate interaction, such as ReportForm; control objects coordinate a use case. A UI form is normally boundary, not entity.SE13

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Actor identification establishes external roles rather than generalizing scenario executions into interaction descriptions.

            B · correct — Use cases abstract related concrete scenarios into structured goal-oriented interaction descriptions.

            C · incorrect — Scenario identification captures concrete executions rather than their use-case abstraction.

            D · incorrect — Refinement elaborates an existing use case; the scenario-to-use-case abstraction is the identification step asked here.

            Question 241

            According to the Simple Use Case Writing Guide, which of the following is CORRECT practice?

            • A. Use passive voice so responsibility is unclear
            • B. Describe user interface elements in detail
            • C. Document exceptions separately from the main flow
            • D. Combine multiple tasks into one use case for brevity

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 13

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE15 · Write a complete use case with alternatives

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE15 · Write a complete use case with alternatives

            Correct answer: C — Document exceptions separately from the main success flow.

            SE15 instructs writers to use active subject–verb steps and separate errors from normal flow. C follows that rule directly. Passive voice hides responsibility, detailed UI design distracts from goal-level behavior, and combining unrelated tasks does not produce a clear use case. The distinction concerns organizing scenarios rather than omitting exception handling.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Example: Submit Incident. Precondition: officer authenticated. 1 Officer supplies location and description. 2 System validates details. 3 System records the incident. 4 System returns its ID. Alternative 2a: location missing → report the problem and request correction; save nothing. Success postcondition: incident and ID persist; failure guarantee: no partial record. An alternate flow is a conditional variation; an exception flow handles a failure. Preconditions hold before entry, while a trigger starts the use case.SE15
            Use active subject–verb steps at one abstraction level; separate errors from the normal flow.SE15

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Passive voice makes responsibility less clear, contrary to the active subject–verb guideline.

            B · incorrect — Detailed UI elements are not the goal-level behavior and flow structure emphasized by the guide.

            C · correct — Separating exception behavior keeps the main success flow clear while still documenting failures.

            D · incorrect — Combining multiple unrelated tasks sacrifices a coherent goal and consistent abstraction level.

            Question 244

            Which validation property ensures that the requirements specification does not contain contradictory statements?

            • A. Completeness
            • B. Consistency
            • C. Clarity
            • D. Correctness

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 16

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

            Study-guide sections

            SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE11 · Validate requirements and maintain traceability

            Correct answer: B — Consistency.

            SE11 directly defines consistency as excluding contradictions. Completeness covers agreed scope, clarity gives one intended interpretation, and correctness reflects stakeholder needs. A specification can be complete yet inconsistent, or clear yet wrong, so these properties cannot substitute for the precise no-contradictions condition.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Correct requirements reflect actual stakeholder needs. Complete requirements address the agreed scope, normal and exceptional behavior. Consistency excludes contradictions. Clarity/unambiguity gives one intended interpretation; feasibility/realism means achievable within constraints. Verifiability means objective evidence can check fulfillment. Replace “fast for most users” with a defined metric, workload and threshold.SE11

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Completeness concerns covering scope and behavior, not whether requirements contradict each other.

            B · correct — Consistency requires the specification’s statements to coexist without contradiction.

            C · incorrect — Clarity addresses interpretive ambiguity rather than logical compatibility between requirements.

            D · incorrect — Correctness concerns actual stakeholder needs, a different validation property.

            Question 245

            The Waterfall model is MOST appropriate when:

            • A. Requirements are expected to change frequently during development
            • B. The project is large and complex with evolving needs
            • C. Requirements are constant, the project is short, and technology is stable
            • D. The team needs to deliver working software in small increments

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 17

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Correct answer: C — Stable requirements and familiar, stable technology.

            SE03 says classical waterfall fits well-understood stable requirements and familiar technology, directly supporting C among these alternatives. Frequent change, evolving needs and early small deliveries call for feedback or incremental capability rather than waterfall’s late feedback. Short duration alone is not a proof, but C also supplies the decisive stability conditions stated in the note.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly. It does not make change physically impossible: real projects revisit work under control, and modified waterfall explicitly includes feedback. Rigidity offers milestone visibility but can freeze incorrect assumptions.SE03

            B · incorrect — Large evolving needs do not establish the stable requirements that favor classical waterfall.

            D · incorrect — Prioritized usable small deliveries are the rationale for incremental delivery rather than a single sequential release.

            Question 247

            What is the key conceptual distinction between iteration and incremental delivery, even when a process combines both?

            • A. Iterative adds new features each cycle; Incremental refines the same set repeatedly
            • B. Iteration revisits and improves a solution; an increment adds usable functionality.
            • C. They are identical; the terms are interchangeable

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 19

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE04 · Iteration, increments and early delivery

            Correct answer: B — Iteration revisits and improves a solution; an increment adds usable functionality.

            Iteration revisits and improves a solution, while an increment adds usable functionality. A process can refine existing capability and add new capability in the same cycle, so the concepts are compatible but not identical. Neither requires rebuilding the entire system or making every increment completely independent. Risk analysis is a separate concern rather than the structural distinction defining these two terms.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Choose incremental delivery when prioritized partial capability must reach users early. Smaller changes can be easier to debug and permit feedback, though architecture and integration still require planning. Iteration need not rebuild the whole system every time, and increments need not be perfectly independent modules. Broad descriptions of early working software can fit prototypes, iterative or Agile processes; identify the purpose of that early version.SE04
            Iteration revisits and improves a solution; an increment adds usable functionality. A process may do both.SE04

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — This reverses refinement and added functionality.

            B · correct — Iteration refines; increments add usable capability.

            C · incorrect — The terms differ even when combined in one process.

            D · incorrect — Risk analysis does not define their distinction.

            Study-guide references

            Correct answer: C — Iterative Model

            The stated emphasis is iterative: revisiting and improving an existing solution in response to feedback. Incremental development names the addition of usable functionality, which is not the primary goal specified, although both can coexist. Large size and anticipated change alone would not have selected a unique model.

            A common lifecycle names requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance.             Iteration revisits and improves a solution; an increment adds usable functionality. A process may do both.SE04

            Correct answer: C — User stories.

            SE05 defines a user story as a small user need and value supported by acceptance criteria. Sprints and iterations name cycles or timeboxes, not the need itself. An epic groups broader work. C therefore names the small functional work unit intended here, without claiming that Agile requirements consist only of story text.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05
            A user story states a small user need and value, supported by acceptance criteria; an epic groups broader work.SE05

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — A Sprint is a timeboxed development interval rather than the individual user need.

            B · incorrect — An iteration is a cycle of work or refinement, not a small functional requirement.

            C · correct — A user story states a small user need and its value with acceptance criteria.

            D · incorrect — An epic groups broader work rather than naming the smaller story-sized need.

            Question 250

            The Spiral Model distinguishes itself from other models primarily through its emphasis on:

            • A. Sequential phase completion
            • B. Risk Analysis at every cycle
            • C. Customer delivery at the end of the project
            • D. Strict adherence to initial requirements

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 22

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE06 · Spiral development and risk

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE06 · Spiral development and risk

            Correct answer: B — Risk analysis and reduction in every spiral cycle.

            SE06 defines spiral development as risk driven, with each cycle identifying objectives and alternatives, assessing and reducing risks, producing a result and planning commitment. That emphasis distinguishes it from merely repeating phases or delivering only at the end. It can adapt requirements and combine other activities rather than enforcing an unchangeable initial specification.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Spiral development is risk driven. Each cycle identifies objectives and alternatives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops/verifies an appropriate next result, and plans further commitment. A prototype may test a risky technology before a large investment. The amount and type of work depend on the risks.SE06

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — A spiral can contain staged work, but sequential completion is not its defining driver.

            B · correct — Risk assessment and reduction guide each cycle’s work and further commitment.

            C · incorrect — Only delivering at the end is not the distinguishing spiral principle.

            D · incorrect — A risk-driven cycle can revise plans and requirements rather than rigidly freeze them.

            Question 251

            The V-Model derives its name from its shape. What does the BOTTOM of the 'V' represent?

            • A. Requirements Gathering
            • B. Deployment
            • C. Coding/Implementation
            • D. Maintenance

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 23

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Correct answer: C — Coding/implementation.

            SE03 explicitly places coding at the bottom of the V while specification and design stages correspond to later testing levels. Requirements therefore begin the development side rather than occupy the bottom; deployment and maintenance are not that connecting implementation activity. This is a model-diagram convention, not a claim that all real work follows a perfect geometric sequence.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            The V-model pairs specification/design stages with later test levels. Requirements inform acceptance tests; system design informs system tests; component/detail design informs integration/unit tests. Coding lies at the bottom. Test planning starts early. Stable requirements and strong assurance may favor this organization, but neither a V shape nor waterfall guarantees safety or correctness.SE03

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Requirements occur on the specification side, not at the coding bottom of the V.

            B · incorrect — Deployment is not the implementation activity joining the V-model’s sides.

            C · correct — The note explicitly identifies coding as the bottom of the V.

            D · incorrect — Maintenance occurs in lifecycle evolution rather than at this implementation point.

            Question 254

            When execution reaches an include relationship’s inclusion point in a base use case, what does include require?

            • A. Optional behavior that may be added to the base use case
            • B. The included behavior is required whenever execution reaches the inclusion point.
            • C. An inheritance relationship between two use cases
            • D. A timing constraint between two use cases

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 26

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

            Correct answer: B — The included behavior is required whenever execution reaches the inclusion point.

            Include factors required reused behavior into another use case. When the base reaches the inclusion point, the included behavior is incorporated and performed as specified. This does not imply that every possible conditional branch of the base reaches that point. Optional conditional additions correspond to extend, specialization to generalization, and timing constraints are separate from the inclusion relationship.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Generalization relates a specialized actor/use case to a more general one, with a hollow triangle toward the general element. An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. It is not defined merely by reuse or lack of a direct actor line. Included behavior is incorporated where the inclusion is reached; do not infer every conditional branch in the base always executes.SE16
            Include factors required reused behavior: Submit Order includes Validate Order, with the dashed arrow from the including/base use case to the included one.SE16

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Conditional optional added behavior describes extend.

            B · correct — The included behavior is required when its inclusion point is reached.

            C · incorrect — Specialization is generalization rather than include.

            D · incorrect — Include is not a timing constraint.

            Question 256

            In UML, which relationship is represented by a HOLLOW diamond shape pointing toward the 'whole' class?

            • A. Composition
            • B. Dependency
            • C. Aggregation
            • D. Generalization

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 28

            SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

            Correct answer: C — Shared aggregation.

            SE18 defines shared aggregation with a hollow diamond at the whole end. Composition instead uses a filled diamond; dependency is a dashed arrow and generalization uses a hollow triangle. The question’s whole-end description is consistent with the notation, so the hollow shape uniquely identifies aggregation among these alternatives.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Composition uses a filled diamond at the whole end and strong ownership: a part is in at most one composite at a time, and parts still owned are destroyed with that composite. Parts may be detached/transferred under a defined model. Thus “cannot ever exist independently” is an oversimplification. For Car composing Engine, the diamond belongs beside Car; saying it points to Engine is imprecise. The Car–Engine example describes composition.SE18
            Shared aggregation uses a hollow diamond at the whole end and weak whole-part meaning;SE18

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Composition uses a filled diamond, not the specified hollow diamond.

            B · incorrect — Dependency is represented by a dashed arrow rather than a whole-part diamond.

            C · correct — Shared aggregation uses a hollow diamond placed at the whole end.

            D · incorrect — Generalization uses a hollow triangle toward the general element rather than a diamond.

            Study-guide references

            SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

            Correct answer: B — Composition has exclusive composite ownership at a time and destroys still-owned parts with the whole; shared aggregation gives weaker whole-part meaning.

            Composition gives strong ownership: a part is in at most one composite at a time, and still-owned parts are destroyed with that composite. Shared aggregation indicates weaker whole-part meaning without that detailed lifecycle policy. A model can permit detachment or transfer, so permanent inability to exist independently is too strong. Neither relationship is inheritance, and composition is not restricted to interfaces.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Composition uses a filled diamond at the whole end and strong ownership: a part is in at most one composite at a time, and parts still owned are destroyed with that composite. Parts may be detached/transferred under a defined model. Thus “cannot ever exist independently” is an oversimplification. For Car composing Engine, the diamond belongs beside Car; saying it points to Engine is imprecise. The Car–Engine example describes composition.SE18

            C · incorrect — Aggregation is not inheritance; generalization is separate.

            D · incorrect — The ownership meanings differ, so they are not synonyms.

            Question 260

            In system design, 'coupling' between subsystems refers to:

            • A. How well objects within a subsystem work toward a common goal
            • B. The number of operations a subsystem exposes
            • C. The degree of dependency between two subsystems
            • D. The architectural pattern chosen for the system

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

            Correct answer: C — The degree of dependency between subsystems.

            SE22 explicitly distinguishes cohesion within a module from coupling between modules. A describes cohesion; C describes coupling. Interface operation count can affect design complexity but is not the definition of dependence, and an architectural pattern may influence coupling without being the relationship measure itself. The goal is usually low coupling with high cohesion.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Related purpose inside a subsystem defines cohesion rather than between-subsystem coupling.

            B · incorrect — Operation count alone does not measure the actual dependencies between subsystems.

            C · correct — Coupling is the degree of dependency between modules or subsystems.

            D · incorrect — An architectural style can affect coupling but is not its definition.

            Question 261

            In architectural design, a 'closed architecture' in a layered system means:

            • A. No external access to any layer is allowed
            • B. A layer can access any layer at deeper levels freely
            • C. A layer can only call the layer immediately below it
            • D. All layers communicate through a central repository

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 33

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

            Study-guide sections

            SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE23 · Layers, tiers and architecture views

            Correct answer: C — Calls are restricted to the immediately lower layer.

            SE23 defines a closed layered architecture as allowing calls only to the immediately lower layer. Open layering may permit approved skipping, so B describes a different policy. Closed does not mean no external access or a shared repository; it concerns permitted dependencies between layers rather than the system’s exposure or storage organization.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A layer is a logical abstraction level; a tier is a deployment separation. A closed layered architecture permits calls only to the immediately lower layer; an open one permits approved skipping. For top-to-bottom A,B,C,D, A→B obeys closed layering, A→C skips, and lower-to-upper calls violate the simple dependency rule unless explicitly mediated by a defined mechanism.SE23

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Closed layering restricts interlayer calls, not every form of external access.

            B · incorrect — Skipping freely to deeper layers contradicts the immediate-lower-layer restriction.

            C · correct — A layer calls only the immediately lower layer in the defined closed architecture.

            D · incorrect — A central repository is another architectural arrangement and does not define closed layering.

            Question 262

            • D. Model-View-Controller Style

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 34

            SE24 · Architecture styles and integration boundaries

            Correct answer: D — Model–View–Controller.

Repository, client–server and peer-to-peer organize central data or interacting roles differently; any may be combined with MVC, but none is the name of this particular three-responsibility separation.

            Repository style shares central data, simplifying common access but creating bottleneck/schema dependencies. MVC separates domain model, display view and interaction controller.             D · correct — Model–View–Controller explicitly names the three responsibilities in the question.

            Study-guide references

            SE17 · Class diagrams, visibility and multiplicity

            Correct answer: C — Zero or more instances.

            SE17 defines 0..* as any nonnegative number. Zero is allowed and the star places no finite upper bound, so C fits. The alternatives correspond to 1, 0..1 and 1..* respectively. Multiplicity at one end is interpreted relative to one object at the opposite end, not as a whole-system object count.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Multiplicity at one end counts how many objects there may correspond to one object at the opposite end: 1 exactly one, 0..1 optional, 0..* any nonnegative number, 1..* at least one. A one-to-many association does not automatically mean composition. Read each end separately before choosing cardinality.SE17

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Exactly one corresponds to multiplicity 1 rather than 0..*.

            B · incorrect — Optional single-valued multiplicity is 0..1, not an unbounded star.

            C · correct — Zero is permitted and the upper star allows any number of related instances.

            D · incorrect — One or more requires lower bound 1, written 1..*.

            Question 268

            In Abbott's heuristics for identifying associations, which phrase pattern most directly suggests a relationship between classes?

            • A. Look for adjective phrases describing class properties
            • B. Examine verb phrases like 'has', 'is part of', 'manages', 'reports to'
            • C. Find all nouns that appear more than twice
            • D. Identify all user interface terms

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 40

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

            Study-guide sections

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Correct answer: B — Verb phrases expressing relationships, such as manages or reports to.

            SE13 recommends nouns as candidate objects and verbs such as manages/reports-to as candidate associations. B is the relationship-phrase option. Adjectives generally describe properties, repeated nouns do not automatically imply an association, and UI terms suggest boundary concerns. These are candidate-identification heuristics rather than a proof that every verb must become a modeled link.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Use nouns as candidate objects, possessive descriptions as candidate attributes, and verbs such as manages/reports-to as candidate associations. These are heuristics, not automatic parsing rules. CRC means Class, Responsibilities, Collaborators. A control per use case or participating actor can be a useful starting point, not a mandatory UML rule or fixed object lifetime.SE13

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Property descriptions suggest attributes rather than directly identifying links between classes.

            B · correct — Relationship verbs are the note’s direct heuristic for candidate associations.

            C · incorrect — Noun frequency is not the stated association-identification rule; nouns instead suggest candidate objects.

            D · incorrect — UI terminology may suggest boundaries but does not directly establish an association between domain classes.

            Question 269

            In software testing, which type of testing evaluates the software's behavior WITHOUT knowledge of its internal code structure?

            • A. White Box Testing
            • B. Grey Box Testing
            • C. Black Box Testing
            • D. Structural Testing

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 41

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

            Study-guide sections

            SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

            Correct answer: C — Black-box testing.

            SE36 contrasts black-box cases derived from required behavior with white-box cases derived from implementation structure. Grey-box uses partial internal knowledge. The question excludes internal-code knowledge, so black-box is the appropriate technique. Structural testing instead refers to the very internal paths or statements that this scenario does not inspect.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Black-box techniques derive cases from specified behavior; white-box techniques derive them from internal structure; grey-box uses partial internal knowledge. Regression testing checks for unintended effects after change; confirmation testing checks the particular defect repair. Exploratory testing combines learning, design and execution and is experience based. Manual/automated describe execution support, not a compulsory black-/white-box classification.SE36

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — White-box testing explicitly uses internal implementation structure to derive cases.

            B · incorrect — Grey-box testing uses partial internal knowledge rather than excluding it.

            C · correct — Black-box testing derives cases from externally specified behavior without needing code structure.

            D · incorrect — Structural testing is based on internal control or code structure, contrary to the stem.

            Question 270

            Which type of functional testing verifies that individual components work correctly in ISOLATION?

            • A. System Testing
            • B. Integration Testing
            • C. Regression Testing
            • D. Unit Testing

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 42

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

            Study-guide sections

            SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE35 · Testing levels and acceptance

            Correct answer: D — Unit testing.

            SE35 defines unit testing as isolating a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs or mocks. Integration checks combined interactions and system testing evaluates the whole system. Regression describes testing after changes and can occur at different levels, so it is not the isolation level named by the question.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component, often replacing dependencies with stubs/mocks; a driver invokes the unit and a stub substitutes a called dependency. Integration testing exercises interfaces and interactions among combined parts. System testing checks the complete integrated system against functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment.SE35

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — System testing evaluates the complete integrated system rather than an isolated component.

            B · incorrect — Integration testing focuses on interactions among combined parts, not isolation.

            C · incorrect — Regression checks unintended effects after change and is not inherently a component-isolation level.

            D · correct — Unit testing evaluates a small component in isolation, with dependencies replaceable by test doubles.

            Question 271

            Non-functional testing that evaluates how the system behaves under expected workloads and measures response speed is called:

            • A. Usability Testing
            • B. Reliability Testing
            • C. Performance Testing
            • D. Compatibility Testing

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 43

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking.

            Study-guide sections

            SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE36 · Test types, regression and exploratory work

            Correct answer: C — Performance testing, specifically load-oriented testing under expected demand.

            SE36 defines performance tests as assessing speed, throughput and resource use under a specified workload and distinguishes expected load from stress beyond normal limits. The stem explicitly adds workload and response speed, so it supports performance testing rather than merely a vague normal-condition test. Usability, reliability and compatibility target different quality questions.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Functional tests check required behavior against the SRS and acceptance criteria. Performance tests assess speed, throughput and resources under a specified workload; load uses expected demands and stress exceeds normal limits. Usability, security, compatibility and reliability tests target their respective qualities. “Normal operating conditions” alone does not distinguish functional from performance testing.SE36

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Usability focuses on task success and ease of use rather than response-speed measurements under load.

            B · incorrect — Reliability concerns failure-free service, not primarily the stated response-time criterion.

            C · correct — Speed under an expected workload is performance/load testing as defined in SE36.

            D · incorrect — Compatibility examines cooperating environments rather than the specified speed-under-load behavior.

            Question 272

            In the analysis phase, which model type uses use cases and scenarios to describe what the software should do?

            • A. Dynamic Model
            • B. Analysis Object Model
            • C. Functional Model
            • D. Structural Model

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 44

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity.

            Study-guide sections

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Correct answer: C — The functional model.

            SE13 explicitly associates use cases and scenarios with functional modeling, classes with structural/object modeling, and states/interactions with dynamic modeling. Thus C names the requested description of what the system should do. The alternatives describe state-dependent behavior or static object structure rather than this user-goal and scenario view.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            A scenario is one concrete execution; a use case abstracts the related successful and alternative scenarios. Analysis integrates functional (use cases/scenarios), structural/object (classes) and dynamic (states/interactions) models. Entity objects represent domain information such as Incident; boundary objects mediate interaction, such as ReportForm; control objects coordinate a use case. A UI form is normally boundary, not entity.SE13

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Dynamic models emphasize states and interactions rather than the named use-case/scenario category.

            B · incorrect — The analysis object model captures classes and relationships rather than the functional use-case view.

            C · correct — Use cases and scenarios are explicitly the functional analysis model.

            D · incorrect — Structural modeling describes static classes and links rather than required user-goal flows.

            Question 273

            In an analysis model, an object coordinates a use case and moves among Idle, WaitingForReply and Completing states as events arrive. Domain entities are passive records and the form has no persistent modes in this scenario. Which object category is the direct state-machine target described?

            • A. Entity Objects
            • B. Boundary Objects
            • C. Control Objects
            • D. All objects equally

            Adapted from

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 45

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE20 · Activity, state and data-flow models

            SE13 · From scenarios to analysis objects

            Correct answer: C — Control Objects

            A control object coordinates a use case, and the described coordinator has significant event-dependent states. A state machine is therefore directly useful for that control object in this scenario. Entities and boundaries can also have meaningful lifecycles in other systems, but here their stated behavior does not supply the modeled states. Suitability follows from responsibilities and lifecycle behavior, not equal need across all objects.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Choose a sequence diagram for message order between participants, a state machine for event-dependent state changes, and activity for workflow. Both sequence and state diagrams describe behavior over time. State machines are useful for objects with significant states, whether entity or control. A DFD shows data stores/flows and transformations from inputs to outputs; it is not a UML diagram.SE20
            A scenario is one concrete execution; a use case abstracts the related successful and alternative scenarios. Analysis integrates functional (use cases/scenarios), structural/object (classes) and dynamic (states/interactions) models. Entity objects represent domain information such as Incident; boundary objects mediate interaction, such as ReportForm; control objects coordinate a use case. A UI form is normally boundary, not entity.SE13

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — The scenario’s entities are passive records rather than the stated coordinator.

            B · incorrect — The form has no persistent modes and is not the use-case coordinator.

            C · correct — The stateful coordinator is a control object.

            D · incorrect — The need depends on significant state behavior, not equality across every object.

            Question 274

            In the ReportEmergency use case example, which boundary object allows the FieldOfficer to initiate the reporting process?

            • A. EmergencyReportForm
            • B. AcknowledgmentNotice
            • C. ReportEmergencyButton
            • D. DispatcherStation

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 46

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

            Correct answer: C — ReportEmergencyButton.

            SE19 explicitly says FieldOfficer activates ReportEmergencyButton, supplies details through EmergencyReportForm and later sees AcknowledgmentNotice. DispatcherStation belongs to the dispatcher side. Therefore the button initiates this particular scenario; the form handles later input and the notice reports completion. This is grounded in the named example rather than a generic rule that every use case starts with a button.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            One interaction-diagram layout heuristic puts the initiating actor first, boundary second, control third, then entities. This is not a required UML column order. In ReportEmergency, FieldOfficer activates ReportEmergencyButton, enters details through EmergencyReportForm, and later sees AcknowledgmentNotice; DispatcherStation belongs to the dispatcher side. Choose the button for initiating this particular scenario.SE19
