            A · incorrect — The form receives incident details after initiation rather than starting the documented scenario.

            B · incorrect — The acknowledgment is seen later as feedback, not used to initiate reporting.

            C · correct — The note explicitly identifies this button as the FieldOfficer’s initiating boundary object.

            D · incorrect — DispatcherStation is on the dispatcher side rather than the FieldOfficer’s initiation interface.

            Question 275

            Generalization in UML modeling is best described as:

            • A. Dividing a class into multiple subclasses with no shared properties
            • B. Identifying a general concept where other concepts are more specific versions of it
            • C. Creating interfaces for external system communication
            • D. Grouping unrelated classes into a package for organization

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 47

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

            SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE18 · Association, aggregation, composition and generalization

            SE16 · Include, extend, generalization and abstract use cases

            Correct answer: B — A general concept with more-specific specializations.

            SE16 relates a specialized actor or use case to a more general one; SE18 gives the corresponding class generalization toward a superclass. B expresses that abstraction/specialization relationship. It does not merely package unrelated classes, create an external interface or split classes while denying shared general properties.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Association connects related instances. A dashed dependency arrow means a client uses a supplier. Generalization uses a solid line and hollow triangle pointing to the superclass/general element. Shared aggregation uses a hollow diamond at the whole end and weak whole-part meaning; it does not by itself define a detailed lifecycle policy.SE18
            Generalization relates a specialized actor/use case to a more general one, with a hollow triangle toward the general element. An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. It is not defined merely by reuse or lack of a direct actor line. Included behavior is incorporated where the inclusion is reached; do not infer every conditional branch in the base always executes.SE16

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Specialization is related through a general concept rather than requiring no shared properties.

            B · correct — Generalization identifies the common general element of which other concepts are more specific versions.

            C · incorrect — External communication interfaces do not by themselves define a generalization relationship.

            D · incorrect — Packaging unrelated classes is organizational grouping rather than specialization of a shared general concept.

            Question 276

            The 'high cohesion, low coupling' principle in subsystem design means:

            • A. Subsystems should be tightly interconnected for maximum communication efficiency
            • B. Objects within a subsystem should be closely related, while subsystems themselves should be mostly independent
            • C. Each subsystem should have minimal internal functionality to reduce complexity
            • D. All subsystems should share a single central data repository

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 48

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits.

            Study-guide sections

            SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE22 · Cohesion, coupling, modularity and refactoring

            Correct answer: B — Related responsibilities within a subsystem, limited dependencies between subsystems.

            SE22 defines cohesion as related purpose within a module and coupling as dependency across modules, then recommends high cohesion and low coupling. B states both dimensions. It does not require minimal functionality, tight cross-connections or one shared repository; those choices can undermine coherent responsibilities or increase dependency rather than establish the principle.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Cohesion measures how well elements inside a module serve a related purpose; coupling measures dependency between modules. Seek high cohesion and low coupling. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s internal representation increase coupling. Information hiding exposes stable operations while concealing changeable decisions.SE22

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Tight interconnection increases coupling rather than meeting the low-coupling goal.

            B · correct — Closely related internal responsibilities and limited external dependencies express both parts of the principle.

            C · incorrect — Cohesion concerns related purpose, not simply having as little functionality as possible.

            D · incorrect — A shared repository is a style choice and can create dependencies; it does not define cohesion or coupling.

            Question 277

            A safety-critical contract requires traceable assurance records and reviewed verification before release. Waterfall, V-model and spiral proposals include those obligations; the proposed lightweight Agile variant supplies working code but omits the required assurance records. Which proposal is least appropriate as specified?

            • A. Waterfall Model
            • B. V-Model
            • C. Agile Model
            • D. Spiral Model

            Adapted from

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 49

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis.

            Study-guide sections

            SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE05 · Agile values, stories and Scrum

            SE03 · Waterfall and the V-model

            Correct answer: C — Agile Model

            The specified Agile proposal omits mandatory assurance records, so it cannot satisfy the stated contract without modification. The other proposals include those obligations and are not excluded on that ground. This is a judgment about the supplied lightweight variant, not Agile in general: the note explicitly allows Agile to incorporate required documentation and assurance. Stable requirements alone would not establish a universal ranking.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Scrum uses timeboxed Sprints of at most one month, with a Sprint Goal, selected work and a usable Increment meeting a Definition of Done. Scope is discussed before and during planning; it is not forbidden to agree scope. Timeboxes tend to stay fixed while content is adapted without endangering the goal. Agile can be combined with required assurance/documentation; safety-critical context alone cannot prove it is unsuitable.SE05
            The V-model pairs specification/design stages with later test levels. Requirements inform acceptance tests; system design informs system tests; component/detail design informs integration/unit tests. Coding lies at the bottom. Test planning starts early. Stable requirements and strong assurance may favor this organization, but neither a V shape nor waterfall guarantees safety or correctness.SE03
            Classical waterfall separates planned phases with reviewed deliverables. It fits well-understood, stable requirements and familiar technology; late feedback makes changes costly.SE03

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — This proposal includes the required reviewed deliverables.

            B · incorrect — This proposal includes the required assurance obligations.

            C · correct — The specified lightweight variant omits mandatory records and is therefore least suitable as proposed.

            D · incorrect — This proposal includes the stated assurance obligations.

            Question 278

            In a sequence diagram, what does an 'X' (cross) at the end of a lifeline dashed line indicate?

            • A. The object is temporarily inactive
            • B. The object is waiting for a message
            • C. The object ceases to exist at that point
            • D. The object is calling itself recursively

            Source

            • Software Engineering review questions · Question 50

            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

            Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it.

            Study-guide sections

            SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

            Answer & Detailed Explanation

            Study-guide references

            SE19 · Sequence diagrams and the emergency-report example

            Correct answer: C — Modeled destruction of the object at that point.

            SE19 explicitly identifies X as modeled destruction, so C is correct in UML diagram semantics. Temporary inactivity and waiting do not end an object’s modeled existence, and a recursive message is represented by an interaction rather than destruction. The marker does not guarantee the runtime moment at which a garbage collector reclaims memory.

            Evidence in the complete study note

            Sequence diagrams show interactions across lifelines, with order/time generally downward. Messages cross between participants; activation rectangles show execution. A creation message starts a lifeline; an X marks modeled destruction, not a guarantee about when a garbage collector runs. Synchronous calls wait for completion; asynchronous messages permit the sender to proceed.SE19

            Choice by choice

            A · incorrect — Temporary inactivity does not terminate the object’s lifeline.

            B · incorrect — Waiting for a message does not mean the modeled object has been destroyed.

            C · correct — X marks the object’s modeled destruction at that point, not necessarily immediate memory reclamation.

            D · incorrect — A recursive call is an interaction message and does not use the destruction marker.
